sentences.zh: 桑喬，字子木，江都人。

translations.literal: Sang Qiao, courtesy name Zimu, was a native of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Qiao, styled Zimu, was a native of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年進士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the eleventh year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 十四年冬，由主事改御史，出按山西。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourteenth year he was transferred from principal clerk to censor and sent on an inspection tour of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourteenth year he was promoted from principal clerk to censor and dispatched to inspect Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 所部頻寇躪，喬奏請盡蠲徭賦，厚恤死者家。

translations.literal: His jurisdiction was repeatedly ravaged by bandits; Qiao memorialized requesting full remission of corvée levies and generous relief for the families of the dead.
translations.idiomatic: His jurisdiction suffered repeated raids, and Qiao memorialized asking that corvée levies be fully remitted and the families of the dead generously compensated.

sentences.zh: 參將葉宗等將萬人至荊家莊，陷賊伏中，大潰，賊遂深入。

translations.literal: The assistant commander Ye Zong and others led ten thousand men to Jingjia Village, fell into an ambush, suffered a great rout, and the bandits then penetrated deep.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Commander Ye Zong and others led ten thousand troops to Jingjia Village, walked into an ambush, and were routed; the bandits then drove deep into the territory.

sentences.zh: 天城、陽和兩月間五遭寇。

translations.literal: Within two months Tiancheng and Yanghe were attacked by bandits five times.
translations.idiomatic: Within two months Tiancheng and Yanghe were raided five times.

sentences.zh: 巡撫樊繼祖、總兵官魯綱以下，皆為喬劾，副將李懋及宗等六人並逮治。

translations.literal: The grand coordinator Fan Jizu, the regional commander Lu Gang, and all below them were impeached by Qiao; the vice-commander Li Mao and Zong and five others were all arrested and tried.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Fan Jizu, Regional Commander Lu Gang, and their subordinates were all impeached by Qiao; Vice-Commander Li Mao, Zong, and five others were arrested and brought to trial.

sentences.zh: 十六年夏，雷震謹身殿，下詔求言。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixteenth year thunder struck the Hall of Self-Cultivation, and an edict was issued soliciting criticism.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixteenth year lightning struck the Hall of Self-Cultivation, and the emperor issued an edict calling for remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 喬偕同官陳三事，略言營造兩宮山陵，多侵冒；

translations.literal: Qiao joined his colleagues in memorializing on three matters, briefly noting that construction of the two palaces and imperial tombs involved much embezzlement;
translations.idiomatic: Qiao joined his fellow censors in a memorial on three matters, briefly noting widespread embezzlement in the construction of the two palaces and imperial tombs;

sentences.zh: 吉囊恣橫，邊備積弛。

translations.literal: Jinang acted with impunity, and frontier defenses had long grown lax.
translations.idiomatic: Jinang ran rampant, and frontier defenses had long been neglected.

sentences.zh: 而末言：「陛下遇災而懼，下詔修省。

translations.literal: At the end he said: "Your Majesty, encountering disaster, became fearful and issued an edict for self-examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the end he wrote: "Your Majesty, shaken by this calamity, has issued an edict calling for self-examination.

sentences.zh: 修省不外人事，人事無過擇官。

translations.literal: Self-examination lies in nothing outside human affairs, and among human affairs nothing surpasses choosing officials.
translations.idiomatic: Self-examination comes down to human affairs, and among human affairs nothing matters more than choosing the right officials.

sentences.zh: 尚書嚴嵩及林庭昂、張瓚、張雲皆上負國恩，下乖輿望，災變之來，由彼所致。

translations.literal: The ministers Yan Song, Lin Tingqi, Zhang Zan, and Zhang Yun all failed the state's grace above and betrayed public expectation below; the calamities arose because of them.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Yan Song, Lin Tingqi, Zhang Zan, and Zhang Yun have all failed the grace of the state above and betrayed public expectation below—these calamities have come because of them.

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，四人皆乞罷。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, all four requested dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, all four men asked to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 詔庭昂、雲致仕，留嵩、瓚如故。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Tingqi and Yun to retire, while Song and Zan were retained as before.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Lin Tingqi and Zhang Yun to retire, while Yan Song and Zhang Zan were kept in office as before.

sentences.zh: 嵩再疏辨，且詆言者。

translations.literal: Song submitted another memorial in self-defense and also slandered the memorializers.
translations.idiomatic: Song submitted another memorial defending himself and also vilified those who had spoken out.

sentences.zh: 給事中胡汝霖言：「大臣被論，引罪求退而已。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Hu Rulin said: "When a grand minister is criticized, he need only acknowledge guilt and request withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Hu Rulin said: "When a grand minister is criticized, he need only accept blame and ask to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 嵩負穢行，召物議，逞辭奏辨，陰擠言官，無大臣體。

translations.literal: Song bears a tainted record, invites public censure, yet uses verbose memorials to argue his case and secretly undermines the remonstrators—this is not the bearing of a grand minister.
translations.idiomatic: Song carries a tainted reputation, invites public censure, yet indulges in wordy self-defense and secretly undermines the remonstrators—this is not how a grand minister should conduct himself.

sentences.zh: 」帝下詔戒飭如汝霖指。

translations.literal: " The emperor issued an edict of admonition along the lines Hu Rulin indicated.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor issued an edict of admonition along the lines Hu Rulin had indicated.

sentences.zh: 時嵩拜尚書甫半歲，方養交遊，揚聲譽，為進取地，舉朝猶未知其奸，喬獨首發之。

translations.literal: At that time Song had been appointed minister for only half a year; he was cultivating connections, burnishing his reputation, and laying groundwork for advancement—the whole court still did not know his treachery, and Qiao alone was first to expose it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Song had been minister for only half a year; he was cultivating allies, burnishing his reputation, and building a path to power—the whole court still did not know his treachery, and Qiao alone was the first to expose it.

sentences.zh: 喬尋巡按畿輔，引疾。

translations.literal: Qiao soon toured the capital region on inspection, then pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao soon undertook an inspection tour of the capital region, then pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 都御史王廷相以規避劾之，嵩因構其罪。

translations.literal: The censor-in-chief Wang Tingxiang impeached him for evasion; Song then fabricated charges against him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wang Tingxiang impeached him for shirking duty, and Song then fabricated charges against him.

sentences.zh: 逮下詔獄，廷杖，戍九江。

translations.literal: He was arrested and sent to the imperial prison, beaten at court, and exiled to Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was arrested and sent to the imperial prison, beaten at court, and exiled to Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 居戍所二十六年而卒。

translations.literal: After dwelling at his place of exile for twenty-six years, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at his place of exile for twenty-six years and then died.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈恤如制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, posthumous honors and relief were granted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign, posthumous honors and relief were granted according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 胡汝霖，綿州人。

translations.literal: Hu Rulin was a native of Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Rulin was a native of Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士除戶科給事中。

translations.literal: From Hanlin bachelor he was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Revenue section.
translations.idiomatic: From his post as Hanlin bachelor he was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Revenue section.

sentences.zh: 二十年四月，九廟災。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twentieth year, the Nine Temples burned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twentieth year, fire destroyed the Nine Temples.

sentences.zh: 偕同官聶靜、御史李乘雲劾文武大臣救火緩慢者二十六人，嵩與焉。

translations.literal: With his colleague Nie Jing and the censor Li Chengyun he impeached twenty-six civil and military grand ministers for sluggishness in firefighting, Yan Song among them.
translations.idiomatic: Together with his colleague Nie Jing and Censor Li Chengyun, he impeached twenty-six civil and military grand ministers for sluggish firefighting, Yan Song among them.

sentences.zh: 帝怒所劾不盡，下詔獄訊治，俱鐫級調外。

translations.literal: The emperor, angered that the impeachment was incomplete, sent them all to the imperial prison for interrogation; all were degraded and transferred outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, angered that the impeachment did not go far enough, sent them all to the imperial prison for interrogation; all were demoted and transferred outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 汝霖得太平府經歷。

translations.literal: Rulin was given the post of assistant prefect of Taiping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Rulin was assigned as assistant prefect of Taiping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既謫官，則請解於嵩，反附以進。

translations.literal: Once demoted, he asked Yan Song for forgiveness and instead attached himself to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Once demoted, he sought Yan Song's forgiveness and instead attached himself to Song in order to rise again.

sentences.zh: 累遷至右僉都御史，巡撫甘肅。

translations.literal: He rose in successive appointments to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he reached the post of Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 及嵩敗，以嵩黨奪官。

translations.literal: When Song fell, he was stripped of office as a member of Song's faction.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Song fell, he was stripped of office as a member of Song's faction.

sentences.zh: 謝瑜，字如卿，上虞人。

translations.literal: Xie Yu, courtesy name Ruqing, was a native of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yu, styled Ruqing, was a native of Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年進士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the eleventh year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 由南京御史改北。

translations.literal: From Nanjing censor he was transferred to the northern capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred from censor at Nanjing to censor at the northern capital.

sentences.zh: 十九年正月，禮部尚書嚴嵩屢被彈劾求去，帝慰留。

translations.literal: In the first month of the nineteenth year, Minister of Rites Yan Song, repeatedly impeached and requesting dismissal, was comforted and retained by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the nineteenth year, Minister of Rites Yan Song, who had been repeatedly impeached and had asked to resign, was comforted and kept in office by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 瑜言：「嵩矯飾浮詞，欺罔君上，箝制言官。

translations.literal: Yu said: "Song uses affected and empty language, deceives his sovereign, and silences remonstrators.
translations.idiomatic: Yu wrote: "Song uses affected and empty language, deceives his sovereign, and muzzles the remonstrators.

sentences.zh: 且援明堂大禮、南巡盛事為解，而謂諸臣中無為陛下任事者，欲以激聖怒。

translations.literal: Moreover he cites the Bright Hall rites and the southern tour as excuses, and says that among the ministers none will serve Your Majesty—seeking to provoke the emperor's anger.
translations.idiomatic: He also cites the Bright Hall rites and the southern tour as excuses, and claims that none of the ministers will serve Your Majesty—seeking to provoke the emperor's anger.

sentences.zh: 奸狀顯然。

translations.literal: His treachery is plainly evident.
translations.idiomatic: His treachery is plainly evident.

sentences.zh: 」帝留疏不下。

translations.literal: " The emperor retained the memorial without acting on it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor kept the memorial and did not act on it.

sentences.zh: 嵩奏辨，且言：「瑜擊臣不已，欲與朝廷爭勝」。

translations.literal: Song submitted a defense, saying: "Yu keeps attacking me without cease, seeking to contend with the court for victory."
translations.idiomatic: Song submitted a defense, saying: "Yu keeps attacking me without cease, as if seeking to prevail over the court itself."

sentences.zh: 帝於是切責瑜，而慰諭嵩甚至。

translations.literal: The emperor then sharply rebuked Yu while comforting Song to an extraordinary degree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sharply rebuked Yu while offering Song extraordinary reassurance.

sentences.zh: 居二歲，竟用嵩為相。

translations.literal: After two years Song was at last made chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Yan Song was at last appointed chief minister.

sentences.zh: 甫逾月，瑜疏言：「武廟盤遊佚樂，邊防宜壞而未甚壞。

translations.literal: Barely a month later Yu memorialized: "Under the Martial Temple the emperor roamed in pleasure, and the frontier defenses should have deteriorated but had not greatly done so.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a month later Yu memorialized: "Under the Martial Temple Emperor the court indulged in pleasure, and the frontier defenses ought to have collapsed but had not yet done so badly.

sentences.zh: 今聖明在上，邊防宜固而反大壞者，大臣謀國不忠，而陛下任用失也。

translations.literal: Now with a sage ruler above, the frontier defenses should be secure yet have instead greatly collapsed—this is because grand ministers are disloyal in planning for the state, and Your Majesty's appointments have been mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Now, under a sage ruler, the frontier defenses ought to be secure yet have instead collapsed—this is because grand ministers are disloyal in governing the state, and Your Majesty's appointments have been mistaken.

sentences.zh: 自張瓚為中樞，掌兵而天下無兵，擇將而天下無將。

translations.literal: Since Zhang Zan took the central command, though he holds authority over troops the realm has no troops; though he selects generals the realm has no generals.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhang Zan took command at the center, though he holds authority over troops the realm has no effective army; though he selects generals the realm has no capable generals.

sentences.zh: 說者謂瓚形貌魁梧，足稱福將。

translations.literal: Some say that Zan's imposing stature suffices to call him a general of good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Some say that Zan's imposing stature alone qualifies him as a general of good fortune.

sentences.zh: 夫誠邊塵不聳，海宇晏然，謂之福可也。

translations.literal: If indeed the frontier were quiet and the realm at peace, one might call that fortune.
translations.idiomatic: If the frontier were truly quiet and the realm at peace, one might call that good fortune.

sentences.zh: 今瓚無功而恩蔭屢加，有罪而褫奪不及，此其福乃一身之福，非軍國之福也。

translations.literal: Now Zan, though without merit, receives repeated enfeoffments of grace, and though guilty suffers no stripping of honors—this fortune is fortune for himself alone, not fortune for army and state.
translations.idiomatic: Now Zan, though without merit, receives repeated honors, and though guilty suffers no punishment—this is fortune for himself alone, not fortune for the army and the state.

sentences.zh: 昔舜誅四兇，萬世稱聖。

translations.literal: In antiquity Shun executed the Four Evils, and for ten thousand generations he has been called sage.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Shun executed the Four Evils, and for ten thousand generations he has been hailed as sage.

sentences.zh: 今瓚與郭勛、嚴嵩、胡守中，聖世之四兇。

translations.literal: Now Zan, together with Guo Xun, Yan Song, and Hu Shouzhong, are the Four Evils of this sage age.
translations.idiomatic: Today Zan, together with Guo Xun, Yan Song, and Hu Shouzhong, are the Four Evils of this age of sage rule.

sentences.zh: 陛下旬月間已誅其二，天下翕然稱聖，何不並此二兇，放之流之，以全帝舜之功也？

translations.literal: Your Majesty within a month has already executed two of them, and the realm unanimously calls you sage—why not together banish or exile these two evils as well, to complete the achievement of Emperor Shun?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has already executed two of them within a month, and the realm unanimously hails your sagacity—why not banish or exile these remaining two evils as well, and complete the achievement of Emperor Shun?

sentences.zh: 大學士翟鑾起廢棄中，授以巡邊之寄，乃優遊曼衍，靡費供億。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhai Luan, raised from disgrace, was entrusted with touring the frontier, yet wandered at leisure in extravagance, squandering vast supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhai Luan, restored from disgrace, was entrusted with touring the frontier, yet wandered at leisure in extravagance and squandered vast supplies.

sentences.zh: 以盛苞苴者為才，獻淫樂者為敬，遂使邊軍益瘠，邊備更弛。

translations.literal: He treated those who offered lavish gifts as talented and those who presented lewd entertainment as respectful, so that frontier troops grew ever weaker and frontier defenses ever laxer.
translations.idiomatic: He treated those who offered lavish bribes as talented and those who presented lewd entertainment as respectful, so that frontier troops grew ever weaker and frontier defenses ever laxer.

sentences.zh: 行邊若此，將焉用之！

translations.literal: To tour the frontier in this fashion—of what use is such a man!
translations.idiomatic: To tour the frontier in this fashion—of what use is such a man!

sentences.zh: 故不清政本，天下必不治也。

translations.literal: Therefore if the root of government is not cleared, the realm will surely not be well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore if the root of government is not cleared, the realm will surely not be well governed.

sentences.zh: 不易本兵，武功必不競也。」

translations.literal: If the minister of war is not changed, military achievement will surely not be pursued."
translations.idiomatic: If the minister of war is not replaced, military strength will surely never be restored."

sentences.zh: 疏入，留不下。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, it was retained without action.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, it was retained without action.

sentences.zh: 嵩復疏辯，帝更慰諭，瑜復被譙讓。

translations.literal: Song again submitted a defense; the emperor again comforted him, and Yu was again rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: Song again submitted a defense; the emperor again reassured him, and Yu was rebuked once more.

sentences.zh: 然是時帝雖響嵩，猶未深罪言者，嵩亦以初得政，未敢顯擠陷，故瑜得居職如故。

translations.literal: Yet at this time, though the emperor sided with Song, he had not yet deeply punished the remonstrators; Song too, having just taken power, did not dare openly frame and ruin them, so Yu was able to remain in office as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at this time, though the emperor sided with Song, he had not yet severely punished the remonstrators; Song too, having just taken power, did not dare openly frame and ruin them, so Yu was able to remain in office as before.

sentences.zh: 未幾，假他事貶其官。

translations.literal: Before long, on a pretext of other matters, his rank was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, on a pretext of other matters, his rank was reduced.

sentences.zh: 又三載，大計，嵩密諷主者黜之。

translations.literal: Three years later, at the grand evaluation, Song secretly hinted to those in charge that he should be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later, at the grand evaluation, Song secretly hinted to those in charge that Yu should be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 比疏上，令如貪酷例除名，瑜遂廢棄，終於家。

translations.literal: When the memorial went up, he was ordered removed from the rolls according to the precedent for the greedy and cruel; Yu was thus cast aside and ended his days at home.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, he was ordered struck from the rolls under the precedent for the greedy and cruel; Yu was thus cast aside and ended his days at home.

sentences.zh: 始瑜之為御史也，武定侯郭勛陳時政，極詆大小諸臣不足任，請復遣內侍出鎮守。

translations.literal: When Yu first served as censor, the Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun presented views on current affairs, vehemently denouncing grand and petty ministers alike as unfit for office and requesting that eunuchs again be dispatched as garrison commanders.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu first served as censor, the Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun presented views on current affairs, vehemently denouncing ministers great and small as unfit for office and requesting that eunuchs again be dispatched as garrison commanders.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the request.

sentences.zh: 瑜抗章奏曰：「勛所論諸事，影響恍惚，而復設鎮守，則其本意所註也。

translations.literal: Yu submitted a forceful memorial saying: "The matters Xun discusses are vague and insubstantial, and to reestablish garrison commanders is the real aim he has in view.
translations.idiomatic: Yu submitted a forceful memorial saying: "The matters Xun discusses are vague and insubstantial, and to reestablish garrison commanders is the real aim he has in view.

sentences.zh: 勛交通內侍，代之營求，利他日重賄。

translations.literal: Xun maintains relations with eunuchs, seeking posts for them on their behalf, to profit from heavy bribes later.
translations.idiomatic: Xun maintains relations with eunuchs, seeking posts for them on their behalf, so that he may profit from heavy bribes later.

sentences.zh: 其言：『官吏貪濁，由陛下無心腹耳目之人在四方』。

translations.literal: He says: 'Officials are greedy and corrupt because Your Majesty has no trusted eyes and ears in the four directions.'
translations.idiomatic: He says: 'Officials are greedy and corrupt because Your Majesty has no trusted eyes and ears throughout the realm.'

sentences.zh: 又曰：『文武懷奸避事，許內臣劾奏，則奸貪自息』。

translations.literal: He also says: 'When civil and military officials harbor treachery and shirk duty, if eunuchs are allowed to impeach them, then treachery and greed will cease of themselves.'
translations.idiomatic: He also says: 'When civil and military officials harbor treachery and shirk duty, if eunuchs are allowed to impeach them, then treachery and greed will cease of themselves.'

sentences.zh: 果若勛言，則內臣用事莫如正德時，其為太平極治耶？

translations.literal: If Xun's words were true, then under no reign were eunuchs more powerful than in the Zhengde era—was that an age of supreme peace and good order?
translations.idiomatic: If Xun's words were true, then under no reign were eunuchs more powerful than in the Zhengde era—was that an age of supreme peace and good order?

sentences.zh: 陛下革鎮守內臣，誠聖明善政，而勛詆以偏私。

translations.literal: Your Majesty abolished garrison eunuchs—a truly sage and enlightened policy—yet Xun denounces this as partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty abolished garrison eunuchs—a truly sage and enlightened policy—yet Xun denounces this as partiality.

sentences.zh: 在朝百官，孰非天子耳目？

translations.literal: Of the hundred officials at court, who is not the Son of Heaven's eyes and ears?
translations.idiomatic: Of the hundred officials at court, who is not the Son of Heaven's eyes and ears?

sentences.zh: 而勛詆以不足任。

translations.literal: Yet Xun denounces them as unfit for office.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xun denounces them as unfit for office.

sentences.zh: 欲陛下盡疑天下士大夫，獨倚宦官為腹心耳目，臣不知勛視陛下為何如主？

translations.literal: He would have Your Majesty distrust all the scholar-officials under Heaven and rely on eunuchs alone as trusted eyes and ears—I do not know what sort of sovereign Xun takes Your Majesty to be.
translations.idiomatic: He would have Your Majesty distrust all scholar-officials under Heaven and rely on eunuchs alone as trusted eyes and ears—I do not know what sort of sovereign Xun takes Your Majesty to be.

sentences.zh: 」會給事中朱隆禧亦以為言，勛奏始寢。

translations.literal: " At the same time Supervising Secretary Zhu Longxi also spoke on the matter, and Xun's memorial was at last shelved.
translations.idiomatic: " At the same time Supervising Secretary Zhu Longxi also spoke on the matter, and Xun's proposal was at last shelved.

sentences.zh: 瑜，隆慶初復官贈太仆少卿。

translations.literal: Yu, at the beginning of Longqing, was restored to office and posthumously given the title Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, at the beginning of the Longqing reign, was restored to office and posthumously given the title Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 王曄，字韜孟，金壇人。

translations.literal: Wang Ye, courtesy name Taomeng, was a native of Jintan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ye, styled Taomeng, was a native of Jintan.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fourteenth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授吉安推官，召拜南京吏科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Ji'an and then summoned to serve as supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel section at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Ji'an and then summoned to serve as supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel section at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 二十年九月偕同官上言：「外寇陸梁，本兵張瓚及總督尚書樊繼祖、新遷侍郎費寀不堪重寄」。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twentieth year he joined his colleagues in memorializing: "Foreign bandits run rampant; Minister of War Zhang Zan, Grand Coordinator Fan Jizu, and the newly transferred Vice Minister Fei Cai are unfit for heavy responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the twentieth year he joined his colleagues in memorializing: "Foreign raiders run rampant; Minister of War Zhang Zan, Grand Coordinator Fan Jizu, and the newly transferred Vice Minister Fei Cai are unfit for such heavy responsibility."

sentences.zh: 帝下其章於所司。

translations.literal: The emperor sent their memorial down to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor referred their memorial to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 居兩月，復劾瓚，因及禮部尚書嚴嵩、總督侍郎胡守中，與巨奸郭勛相結納。

translations.literal: Two months later he again impeached Zan, and by extension Minister of Rites Yan Song and Grand Coordinator Vice Minister Hu Shouzhong, who were in league with the great villain Guo Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Two months later he again impeached Zan, and by extension Minister of Rites Yan Song and Grand Coordinator Vice Minister Hu Shouzhong, who were in league with the great villain Guo Xun.

sentences.zh: 嵩所居第宅，則勛私人代營之。

translations.literal: The residence in which Song lived was built on his behalf by Xun's private agents.
translations.idiomatic: The mansion Yan Song occupied had been built for him by Guo Xun's private agents.

sentences.zh: 逾月，御史伊敏生、鄭蕓、陳策亦雲嵩居宅乃勛私人孫澐所居，澐籍沒，嵩第應在籍中。

translations.literal: A month later, Censors Yi Minsheng, Zheng Yun, and Chen Ce also reported that Song's dwelling was in fact the residence of Xun's private associate Sun Yun; Yun's property had been confiscated, and Song's mansion ought to have been included in the registry.
translations.idiomatic: A month later, Censors Yi Minsheng, Zheng Yun, and Chen Ce also reported that Song's residence was actually the house of Guo Xun's associate Sun Yun; since Yun's property had been confiscated, Song's mansion should have been listed among the seized assets.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，奪敏生等俸一級。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and stripped Minsheng and the others of one grade of salary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and docked Minsheng and the others one salary grade.

sentences.zh: 嵩不問，而守中竟由曄疏獲罪。

translations.literal: Song was not investigated, but Shouzhong in the end was punished because of Ye's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song went untouched, but Hu Shouzhong was ultimately punished because of Wang Ye's memorial.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，嵩入內閣。

translations.literal: The next autumn Song entered the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn, Yan Song entered the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 吏科都給事中沈良才、御史喻時等交章劾嵩。

translations.literal: Shen Liangcai, chief supervising secretary of the Personnel section, Censor Yu Shi, and others submitted successive memorials impeaching Song.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Liangcai, chief supervising secretary of the Personnel section, Censor Yu Shi, and others submitted a stream of memorials impeaching Yan Song.

sentences.zh: 逾月，山西巡按童漢臣章上。

translations.literal: A month later the memorial of Tong Hanchen, touring inspector of Shanxi, was submitted.
translations.idiomatic: A month later a memorial from Tong Hanchen, touring inspector of Shanxi, reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 又逾月，曄與同官陳塏、御史陳紹等章亦上。

translations.literal: Another month later, memorials from Ye together with his colleague Chen Kai and Censor Chen Shao and others were also submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Another month later, memorials from Wang Ye, his colleague Chen Kai, Censor Chen Shao, and others also reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 大指皆論嵩奸貪，而曄疏並及嵩子世蕃，語尤剴切，帝皆不省。

translations.literal: The main thrust of all was to denounce Song's treachery and greed; Ye's memorial also implicated Song's son Shifan, and the language was especially incisive—the emperor paid heed to none of it.
translations.idiomatic: All chiefly condemned Yan Song's treachery and corruption; Wang Ye's memorial also targeted Song's son Shifan, and its language was especially cutting. The emperor took no notice of any of it.

sentences.zh: 嵩憾甚，未有以中也。

translations.literal: Song harbored deep resentment but had no means to trap him.
translations.idiomatic: Song hated him bitterly but had no way to get at him.

sentences.zh: 久之，為山東僉事，給由入都，道病後期，嵩遂奪其官。

translations.literal: After some time, having become Shandong vice commissioner, he presented his credentials to enter the capital, fell ill on the road, and arrived late; Song then stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually, while serving as Shandong vice commissioner, he fell ill en route while traveling to the capital to present his credentials and arrived late; Song then stripped him of his post.

sentences.zh: 曄在臺，嘗劾罷方面官三十九人，直聲甚著。

translations.literal: While Ye was at the censorate, he had once impeached and removed thirty-nine regional officials; his reputation for integrity was very great.
translations.idiomatic: During his time at the censorate, Wang Ye had impeached and removed thirty-nine regional officials; his reputation for plainspoken integrity was widely renowned.

sentences.zh: 比歸，環堵蕭然，數年卒。

translations.literal: When he returned home, his bare walls stood desolate; he died several years later.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned home he lived in bare poverty; he died a few years later.

sentences.zh: 伊敏生，上元人。

translations.literal: Yi Minsheng was a native of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Minsheng was a native of Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 鄭蕓、陳策，俱莆田人。

translations.literal: Zheng Yun and Chen Ce were both natives of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yun and Chen Ce were both natives of Putian.

sentences.zh: 敏生官至山東參政。

translations.literal: Minsheng rose to the post of Shandong administrating commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Minsheng rose to the post of Shandong administrating commissioner.

sentences.zh: 策，臺州知府。

translations.literal: Ce [served as] prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ce served as prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 蕓，終御史。

translations.literal: Yun ended as censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yun ended his career as a censor.

sentences.zh: 沈良才，泰州人。

translations.literal: Shen Liangcai was a native of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Liangcai was a native of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 起家庶吉士，歷官至兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He began his career as a Hanlin bachelor and rose through posts to vice minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a Hanlin bachelor and rose through the ranks to vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 三十六年大計自陳，已調南京矣，嵩附批南京科道拾遺疏中，落其職。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, at the grand review he submitted self-recommendation; he had already been transferred to Nanjing; Song attached a comment to the Nanjing censorate memorial on overlooked officials and had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: At the grand review in the thirty-sixth year he submitted a self-recommendation; though he had already been transferred to Nanjing, Song added a comment to a Nanjing censorate memorial on overlooked officials and had him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 喻時，光山人。

translations.literal: Yu Shi was a native of Guangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shi was a native of Guangshan.

sentences.zh: 官至南京兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He rose to vice minister of War at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of War at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 童漢臣，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Tong Hanchen was a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Hanchen was a native of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 由魏縣知縣入為御史。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Wei County he entered service as censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a censor after serving as magistrate of Wei County.

sentences.zh: 寇大入宣府、大同，總督樊繼祖等掩敗，三以捷聞。

translations.literal: When bandits raided deeply into Xuanfu and Datong, Grand Coordinator Fan Jizu and others concealed defeat and three times reported victories.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders drove deep into Xuanfu and Datong, Grand Coordinator Fan Jizu and others covered up their defeats and three times reported victories.

sentences.zh: 漢臣等劾之，得罪。

translations.literal: Hanchen and others impeached them and were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Hanchen and his colleagues impeached them and were themselves punished.

sentences.zh: 其按山西，督諸將擊卻俺答之薄太原者，會方劾嵩，觸其怒。

translations.literal: When he inspected Shanxi, he directed the generals to repel Altan as he pressed close to Taiyuan; it happened that he was then impeaching Song, provoking Song's anger.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting Shanxi he directed the generals who repelled Altan's advance on Taiyuan; because he was then impeaching Yan Song, he provoked Song's wrath.

sentences.zh: 明年，漢臣與巡撫李玨覈上繼祖等失事狀。

translations.literal: The next year Hanchen and Grand Coordinator Li Jue verified and reported the failures of Jizu and others.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Hanchen and Grand Coordinator Li Jue verified and submitted a report on the failures of Fan Jizu and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 章下吏部。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 漢臣前劾嵩並劾吏部尚書許贊，贊亦憾漢臣。

translations.literal: Hanchen had earlier impeached Song and also impeached Minister of Personnel Xu Zan; Xu likewise resented Hanchen.
translations.idiomatic: Hanchen had earlier impeached Yan Song and also impeached Minister of Personnel Xu Zan, who likewise bore a grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 因言漢臣劾遲延，宜並論。

translations.literal: He then said Hanchen had delayed in impeaching them and that both should be judged together.
translations.idiomatic: He then argued that Hanchen had been slow to impeach them and that both men should be punished together.

sentences.zh: 嵩遂擬旨鐫玨一階留任，謫漢臣湖廣布政司都事。

translations.literal: Song then drafted a rescript cutting Jue one rank but keeping him in office, and demoting Hanchen to director under the Huguang provincial administration commission.
translations.idiomatic: Song then drafted a rescript demoting Li Jue one rank but keeping him in office, and banishing Hanchen to the post of director under the Huguang provincial administration commission.

sentences.zh: 舉朝皆知為嵩所中，莫能救也。

translations.literal: The whole court knew he had been trapped by Song, and no one could save him.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court knew Song had trapped him, and no one could intervene.

sentences.zh: 久之，為泉州知府。

translations.literal: After some time he served as prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 倭賊薄城，有保障功。

translations.literal: When Japanese pirates pressed close to the city, he had merits in its defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Japanese pirates threatened the city, he distinguished himself in its defense.

sentences.zh: 終江西副使。

translations.literal: He ended as vice commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as vice commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 陳塏，余姚人。

translations.literal: Chen Kai was a native of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kai was a native of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 後為嵩斥罷。

translations.literal: Later he was denounced and dismissed by Song.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was denounced and dismissed by Yan Song.

sentences.zh: 何維柏，字喬仲，南海人。

translations.literal: He Weibai, courtesy name Qiaozhong, was a native of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: He Weibai, styled Qiaozhong, was a native of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fourteenth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，授御史。

translations.literal: Selected as a Hanlin bachelor, he was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a Hanlin bachelor, he was appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 雷震謹身殿，維柏言四海困竭，所在流移，而所司議加賦，民不為盜不止。

translations.literal: When thunder struck the Hall of Self-Cultivation, Weibai said the four seas were exhausted and depleted, people were displaced everywhere, yet the responsible offices proposed increasing levies—unless the people become bandits the disorder will not stop.
translations.idiomatic: When thunder struck the Hall of Self-Cultivation, Weibai said the realm was exhausted, people were displaced everywhere, yet the responsible offices proposed raising taxes—unless the people turn to banditry, the unrest will never end.

sentences.zh: 因請罷沙河行宮、金山功德寺工作，及安南問罪之師。

translations.literal: He therefore requested cessation of work on the Shahe traveling palace and Jinshan Temple of Merits, and of the punitive expedition against Annam.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore asked that work be halted on the Shahe traveling palace and the Jinshan Temple of Merits, and that the punitive expedition against Annam be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 帝頗嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor quite appreciatively accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the advice with considerable approval.

sentences.zh: 尋引疾歸。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he cited illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 久之，起巡按福建。

translations.literal: After some time he was raised to inspect Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was recalled to serve as touring inspector of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 二十四年五月疏劾大學士嚴嵩奸貪罪，比之李林甫、盧杞。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-fourth year he memorialized impeaching Grand Secretary Yan Song for treachery and corruption, comparing him to Li Linfu and Lu Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twenty-fourth year he submitted a memorial impeaching Grand Secretary Yan Song for treachery and corruption, comparing him to Li Linfu and Lu Qi.

sentences.zh: 且言嵩進顧可學、盛端明修合方藥，邪媚要寵。

translations.literal: He also said Song had advanced Gu Kexue and Sheng Duanming to compound prescription drugs—a wicked flattery to win favor.
translations.idiomatic: He also charged that Song had promoted Gu Kexue and Sheng Duanming to compound elixirs for him, a corrupt flattery meant to win imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，遣官逮治。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and dispatched officials to arrest and try him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and dispatched officials to arrest and prosecute him.

sentences.zh: 士民遮道號哭，維柏意氣自如。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners blocked the road weeping; Weibai remained composed in spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners blocked the road in tears, but Weibai remained calm and unshaken.

sentences.zh: 下詔獄，廷杖，除名。

translations.literal: He was sent to the prison for edict cases, beaten at court, and stricken from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to the prison for edict cases, beaten at court, and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 家居二十余年。

translations.literal: He lived at home for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 隆慶改元，召復官，擢大理少卿。

translations.literal: At the change of era to Longqing he was summoned back to office and promoted to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When the Longqing reign began, he was recalled to office and promoted to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 遷左僉都御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to left vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 疏請日禦便殿，召執政大臣謀政事，並擇大臣有才德者與講讀儒臣更番入直。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking that the emperor daily attend the informal hall, summon chief ministers to deliberate on government affairs, and additionally select talented and virtuous grand ministers together with lecturing Confucian scholars to rotate in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking that the emperor daily hold court in the informal hall, summon the chief ministers to deliberate on state affairs, and select talented and virtuous senior officials together with lecturing Confucian scholars to rotate in attendance.

sentences.zh: 宮中燕居，慎選謹厚內侍調護聖躬，俾遊處有常，幸禦有節。

translations.literal: For daily life within the palace, carefully select prudent and sincere inner eunuchs to attend the imperial person, so that diversions have regularity and access to consorts has limits.
translations.idiomatic: For daily life within the palace, he urged careful selection of prudent and trustworthy inner eunuchs to attend the emperor, so that his leisure had fixed limits and his visits to the consorts were restrained.

sentences.zh: 非隆冬盛寒，毋輟朝講。

translations.literal: Except in deepest winter and bitter cold, do not cease the morning lectures.
translations.idiomatic: Except in the depths of winter, morning lectures should not be suspended.

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: The memorial was acknowledged.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was acknowledged.

sentences.zh: 進左副都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to left assistant censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left assistant censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，還朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wanli reign he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 歷吏部左、右侍郎，極論鬻官之害。

translations.literal: He served successively as left and right vice minister of Personnel and argued forcefully against the harms of selling offices.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as left and right vice minister of Personnel and spoke out forcefully against the evils of selling offices.

sentences.zh: 御史劉臺劾大學士張居正，居正乞罷，維柏倡九卿留之。

translations.literal: Censor Liu Tai impeached Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng; Juzheng requested dismissal; Weibai led the nine ministers in asking that he be retained.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Liu Tai impeached Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng and Juzheng asked to resign, Weibai led the nine ministers in urging that he be kept in office.

sentences.zh: 及居正遭父喪，詔吏部諭留。

translations.literal: When Juzheng suffered his father's death, an edict ordered the Ministry of Personnel to instruct him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: When Juzheng's father died, an edict ordered the Ministry of Personnel to instruct him to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 尚書張瀚叩維柏，維柏曰：「天經地義，何可廢也？

translations.literal: Minister Zhang Han consulted Weibai; Weibai said: "Heaven's constant and earth's righteousness—how can these be abandoned?
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhang Han pressed Weibai for his view; Weibai said: "Heaven's fixed order and earth's righteousness—how can those be cast aside?

sentences.zh: 」瀚從之而止。

translations.literal: " Han followed him and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " Han took his cue and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 居正怒，取旨罷瀚，停維柏俸三月。

translations.literal: Juzheng was angry, obtained a rescript dismissing Han, and suspended Weibai's salary for three months.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng was furious; he obtained a rescript dismissing Han and suspended Weibai's salary for three months.

sentences.zh: 旋出為南京禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as minister of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was posted out as minister of Rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 考察自陳，居正從中罷之。

translations.literal: At the performance review he submitted self-recommendation; Juzheng intervened and had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: At the performance review he submitted a self-recommendation, but Juzheng intervened and had him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 卒謚端恪。

translations.literal: Upon death he was given the posthumous title Duankete.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was given the posthumous title Duankete (Upright and Respectful).

sentences.zh: 徐學詩，字以言，上虞人。

translations.literal: Xu Xueshi, courtesy name Yiyan, was a native of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xueshi, styled Yiyan, was a native of Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twenty-third year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事，歷郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments and served through to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments and rose to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，俺答薄京師。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Altan pressed close to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year Altan pressed close to the capital.

sentences.zh: 既退，詔廷臣陳制敵之策。

translations.literal: After he withdrew, an edict ordered court ministers to present strategies for controlling the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: After the raiders withdrew, an edict ordered court ministers to submit strategies for dealing with the enemy.

sentences.zh: 諸臣多掇細事以應。

translations.literal: Most ministers picked up trivial matters in response.
translations.idiomatic: Most ministers responded with petty suggestions.

sentences.zh: 學詩憤然曰：「大奸柄國，亂之本也。

translations.literal: Xueshi said angrily: "A great villain holds the reins of state—that is the root of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Xueshi said in anger: "A great villain holds the reins of state—that is the root of disorder.

sentences.zh: 亂本不除，能攘外患哉？

translations.literal: If the root of disorder is not removed, how can external threats be repelled?
translations.idiomatic: If the root of disorder is not removed, how can we repel external threats?

sentences.zh: 」即上疏言：

translations.literal: " He immediately submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 大學士嵩輔政十載，奸貪異甚。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Song has aided governance for ten years; treachery and greed beyond the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yan Song has held power for ten years, and his treachery and greed are extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 內結權貴，外比群小。

translations.literal: Within he binds himself to powerful nobles; without he associates with petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Within the court he binds himself to the powerful; without he consorts with petty men.

sentences.zh: 文武遷除，率邀厚賄，致此輩掊克軍民，釀成寇患。

translations.literal: Civil and military appointments and removals mostly demand heavy bribes, causing these men to squeeze soldiers and civilians and brew bandit trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military appointments and removals mostly require heavy bribes, enabling such men to squeeze soldiers and civilians and breed the very banditry that now plagues the realm.

sentences.zh: 國事至此，猶敢謬引佳兵不祥之說，以謾清問。

translations.literal: When state affairs have come to this, they still dare falsely cite the saying that fine weapons are inauspicious to deceive the clear inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: With the state in this condition, they still dare falsely invoke the saying that fine weapons are inauspicious, so as to deceive Your Majesty's clear inquiry.

sentences.zh: 近因都城有警，密輸財賄南還。

translations.literal: Recently, because the capital was alarmed, he secretly sent wealth and bribes back south.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, when the capital was threatened, he secretly shipped his wealth and bribes back south.

sentences.zh: 大車數十乘，樓船十余艘，水陸載道，駭人耳目。

translations.literal: Dozens of large carts, more than ten tower ships—land and water filled the roads, shocking all who saw and heard.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of large carts and more than ten tower ships filled the roads by land and water, shocking all who witnessed it.

sentences.zh: 又納奪職總兵官李鳳鳴二千金，使鎮薊州，受老廢總兵官郭琮三千金，使督漕運。

translations.literal: He also accepted two thousand in gold from dismissed regional commander Li Fengming to have him stationed at Jizhou, and received three thousand in gold from aged and dismissed regional commander Guo Cong to have him supervise grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: He also accepted two thousand in gold from the dismissed regional commander Li Fengming to restore him to command at Jizhou, and three thousand in gold from the aged and dismissed regional commander Guo Cong to put him in charge of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 諸如此比，難可悉數。

translations.literal: Instances like these are too many to enumerate.
translations.idiomatic: Cases like these are too numerous to count.

sentences.zh: 舉朝莫不嘆憤，而無有一人敢牴牾者，誠以內外盤結，上下比周，積久勢成。

translations.literal: The whole court sighs in outrage, yet not one person dares openly oppose him—truly because inner and outer circles are intertwined, high and low collude, and over time the momentum has hardened.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court sighs in outrage, yet not one person dares openly oppose him—because inner and outer factions are intertwined, high and low collude, and over time their power has become entrenched.

sentences.zh: 而其子世蕃又兇狡成性，擅執父權。

translations.literal: Moreover his son Shifan is vicious and cunning by nature and arrogates his father's authority.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover his son Shifan is vicious and cunning by nature and wields his father's power as his own.

sentences.zh: 凡諸司奏請，必先白其父子，然後敢聞於陛下。

translations.literal: Whatever memorials the various offices submit must first be reported to father and son; only then may they be brought before Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever memorials the various offices submit must first be cleared with father and son; only then may they be brought before Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 陛下亦安得而盡悉之乎？

translations.literal: How then can Your Majesty fully know of them all?
translations.idiomatic: How then can Your Majesty fully know what is happening?

sentences.zh: 蓋嵩權力足以假手下石，機械足以先發制人，勢利足以廣交自固，文詞便給足以掩罪飾非。

translations.literal: For Song's power is enough to employ others to strike a man when he is down; his scheming enough to strike first and control others; his influence and profit enough to form wide associations and secure himself; his fluent words enough to cover crimes and gloss over wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: For Song's power is enough to make others strike a man when he is down; his scheming enough to strike first and control others; his influence and profit enough to build wide alliances and secure himself; his fluent words enough to cover crimes and gloss over wrongs.

sentences.zh: 而精悍警敏，揣摩巧中，足以趨利避害；

translations.literal: He is sharp, alert, and keen; skilled at probing and hitting the mark, enough to pursue profit and avoid harm.
translations.idiomatic: He is sharp, alert, and keen; skilled at reading motives and hitting his mark, enough to pursue profit and avoid harm.

sentences.zh: 彌縫缺失，私交密惠，令色脂言，又足以結人歡心，箝人口舌。

translations.literal: He patches gaps, offers private favors and secret benefits, wears a pleasant face and speaks with oily flattery—also enough to win people's hearts and seal their mouths.
translations.idiomatic: He patches over gaps, dispenses private favors and secret benefits, wears a pleasant face and speaks with oily flattery—enough to win men's hearts and seal their mouths.

sentences.zh: 故前後論嵩者，嵩雖不能顯禍之於正言之時，莫不假事托人陰中之於遷除考察之際。

translations.literal: Therefore those who earlier denounced Song—though Song cannot openly ruin them at the moment they speak plainly—never fails to use pretexts and agents to strike at them secretly during transfers, dismissals, and evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore those who denounce Song—though he cannot openly ruin them at the moment they speak out—always finds pretexts and agents to strike at them secretly during transfers, dismissals, and performance reviews.

sentences.zh: 如前給事中王曄、陳塏，御史謝瑜、童漢臣輩，於時亦蒙寬宥，而今皆安在哉？

translations.literal: Such as the former supervising secretaries Wang Ye and Chen Kai, censors Xie Yu and Tong Hanchen and the like—they were spared at the time, yet where are they now?
translations.idiomatic: Such as the former supervising secretaries Wang Ye and Chen Kai and the censors Xie Yu and Tong Hanchen—they were spared at the time, yet where are they now?

sentences.zh: 陛下誠罷嵩父子，別簡忠良代之，外患自無不寧矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly dismisses Song and his son and separately selects loyal and good men to replace them, external threats will naturally be settled without difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly dismisses Song and his son and selects loyal and capable men to replace them, external threats will naturally be brought under control.

sentences.zh: 帝覽奏，頗感動。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and was quite moved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 方士陶仲文密言嵩孤立盡忠，學詩特為所私修隙耳。

translations.literal: The alchemist Tao Zhongwen secretly said Song stood alone in utmost loyalty, and Xueshi had merely nursed a private grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: But the alchemist Tao Zhongwen secretly told the emperor that Song stood alone in utmost loyalty, and that Xueshi had merely nursed a private grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 帝於是發怒，下之詔獄。

translations.literal: The emperor then grew angry and had him sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then flew into a rage and had him sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 嵩不自安，求去，帝優詔慰諭。

translations.literal: Song felt ill at ease, asked to leave office, and the emperor comforted and reassured him with a gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song felt uneasy and asked to resign, but the emperor comforted and reassured him with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 嵩疏謝，佯為世蕃乞回籍，帝亦不許。

translations.literal: Song submitted a memorial of thanks, feigning to beg on Shifan's behalf to return to his native place; the emperor also did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song submitted a memorial of thanks, feigning to plead on Shifan's behalf to return to his native district; the emperor would not permit that either.

sentences.zh: 學詩竟削籍。

translations.literal: Xueshi was ultimately stripped of his name from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xueshi was ultimately stripped from the official rolls.

sentences.zh: 先劾嵩者葉經、謝瑜、陳紹與學詩皆同里，時稱「上虞四諫」。

translations.literal: Ye Jing, Xie Yu, and Chen Shao, who had earlier impeached Song, together with Xueshi were all fellow townsmen; they were called at the time the "Four Remonstrators of Shangyu."
translations.idiomatic: Ye Jing, Xie Yu, and Chen Shao, who had earlier impeached Yan Song, together with Xu Xueshi were all from the same town; they were known at the time as the "Four Remonstrators of Shangyu."

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，起學詩南京通政參議。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, Xueshi was recalled as vice commissioner of the Nanjing Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign, Xu Xueshi was recalled to serve as vice commissioner of the Nanjing Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 未之官，卒。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, he died.

sentences.zh: 贈大理少卿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 初，學詩族兄應豐以善書擢中書舍人，供事無逸殿，悉嵩所為。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xueshi's clansman elder cousin Yingfeng, for excellence in calligraphy, was promoted to secretary draftsman in the Secretariat, serving in the Hall of Untiring Devotion—all was Song's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xu Xueshi's elder clansman cousin Yingfeng, celebrated for his calligraphy, had been promoted to secretary draftsman in the Secretariat and assigned to the Hall of Untiring Devotion—all through Yan Song's patronage.

sentences.zh: 嵩疑學詩疏出應豐指，會考察，屬吏部斥之。

translations.literal: Song suspected Xueshi's memorial came at Yingfeng's direction; when the time came for the evaluation, he had the Ministry of Personnel dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song suspected Xu Xueshi's memorial had been instigated by Yingfeng; when the routine evaluation came around, he arranged for the Ministry of Personnel to dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 應豐詣迎和門辭，特旨留用，嵩恚益甚。

translations.literal: Yingfeng went to Yinghe Gate to take leave, but a special edict ordered him retained in office; Song's resentment grew even fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Yingfeng went to Yinghe Gate to bid farewell, but a special edict ordered him retained in office; Yan Song's resentment grew even fiercer.

sentences.zh: 居數年以誤寫科書譖於帝，竟杖殺之。

translations.literal: After several years in office, Song slandered him to the emperor for mistakenly copying an examination book, and in the end had him beaten to death with the rod.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later Yan Song slandered him to the emperor for having copied an examination book incorrectly, and ultimately had him beaten to death with the rod.

sentences.zh: 陳紹終韶州知府。

translations.literal: Chen Shao ended his career as prefect of Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shao eventually served as prefect of Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 厲汝進，字子修，灤州人。

translations.literal: Li Rujin, courtesy name Zixiu, was a native of Luanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rujin, styled Zixiu, was a native of Luanzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年進士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the eleventh year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授池州推官，征拜吏科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of Chizhou and was summoned to serve as supervising secretary in the Personnel section of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor of Chizhou and was summoned to serve as supervising secretary in the Personnel section of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 湖廣巡撫陸傑以顯陵工成，召為工部等郎。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Lu Jie of Huguang, because construction at the Xian Mausoleum was completed, had him summoned to serve as a secretary in the Ministry of Works and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Because construction at the Xian Mausoleum was complete, Grand Coordinator Lu Jie of Huguang had him summoned to serve as a secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 汝進言傑素犯清議，不宜佐司空，並劾尚書甘為霖、樊繼祖不職。

translations.literal: Rujin said Jie had long offended clear public opinion and was unfit to assist the Minister of Works; he also impeached the ministers Gan Weilin and Fan Jizu for neglect of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rujin argued that Lu Jie had long offended public opinion and was unfit to assist the Minister of Works; he also impeached the ministers Gan Weilin and Fan Jizu for neglect of duty.

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: The proposal was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took no notice.

sentences.zh: 三遷至戶科都給事中。

translations.literal: After three promotions he reached chief supervising secretary in the Revenue section.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he rose to chief supervising secretary in the Revenue section.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書王杲下獄，汝進與同官海寧查秉彜、馬平徐養正、巴縣劉起宗、章丘劉祿合疏言：「兩淮副使張祿遣使入都，廣通結納。

translations.literal: When Minister of Revenue Wang Gao was imprisoned, Rujin together with his colleagues Zha Bingyi of Haining, Xu Yangzheng of Maping, Liu Qizong of Baxian, and Liu Lu of Zhangqiu jointly submitted a memorial stating: "The vice commissioner of the two Huai regions, Zhang Lu, sent envoys to the capital to cultivate connections widely.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Revenue Wang Gao was imprisoned, Li Rujin together with his colleagues Zha Bingyi of Haining, Xu Yangzheng of Maping, Liu Qizong of Baxian, and Liu Lu of Zhangqiu jointly submitted a memorial stating: "The vice commissioner of the two Huai regions, Zhang Lu, sent envoys to the capital to cultivate connections far and wide.

sentences.zh: 如太常少卿嚴世蕃、府丞胡奎等，皆承賂受囑有證。

translations.literal: Such as Vice Minister of Ceremonies Yan Shifan, assistant prefect Hu Kui, and others—all received bribes and carried out commissions, and there is proof.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Vice Minister of Ceremonies Yan Shifan and Assistant Prefect Hu Kui received bribes and carried out commissions on his behalf, and there is proof of it.

sentences.zh: 世蕃竊弄父權，嗜賄張焰。

translations.literal: Shifan usurps and manipulates his father's authority, and his greed for bribes burns bright.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan usurps and manipulates his father's authority, and his greed for bribes knows no bounds.

sentences.zh: 」詞連倉場尚書王暐。

translations.literal: " The memorial also implicated Minister of Granary Wang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial also implicated Minister of Granary Wang Hui.

sentences.zh: 嵩上疏自理，且求援於中官以激帝怒。

translations.literal: Song submitted a memorial explaining himself and also sought aid from the eunuchs to provoke the emperor's anger.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song submitted a memorial in his own defense and also enlisted the eunuchs to provoke the emperor's anger.

sentences.zh: 帝責其代杲解釋，命廷杖汝進八十，余六十，並謫雲南、廣西典史。

translations.literal: The emperor charged them with explaining matters on Gao's behalf, ordered court beating of Rujin eighty strokes and the others sixty, and demoted them all to record keepers in Yunnan and Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor charged them with having spoken on Wang Gao's behalf, ordered Li Rujin beaten eighty strokes at court and the others sixty, and demoted them all to record keepers in Yunnan and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 明年，嵩復假考察，奪汝進職。

translations.literal: The next year Song again used the evaluation as a pretext and stripped Rujin of his office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Yan Song again used the routine evaluation as a pretext to strip Li Rujin of his office.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，起故官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was recalled to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign he was recalled to his former office.

sentences.zh: 未至京，卒。

translations.literal: Before reaching the capital he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could reach the capital, he died.

sentences.zh: 秉彜由黃州推官歷戶科左給事中。

translations.literal: Bingyi rose from investigating censor of Huangzhou through to left supervising secretary in the Revenue section.
translations.idiomatic: Zha Bingyi rose from investigating censor of Huangzhou to left supervising secretary in the Revenue section.

sentences.zh: 數建白時事。

translations.literal: He repeatedly offered proposals on current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly offered proposals on current affairs.

sentences.zh: 終順天府尹。

translations.literal: He ended his career as prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually served as prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 養正以庶吉士歷戶科右給事中。

translations.literal: Yangzheng rose from Hanlin bachelor through to right supervising secretary in the Revenue section.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yangzheng rose from Hanlin bachelor to right supervising secretary in the Revenue section.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中，官至南京工部尚書。

translations.literal: During Longqing he reached the post of minister of Works at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longqing reign he rose to minister of Works at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 起宗初除衢州推官。

translations.literal: Qizong was first appointed investigating censor of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qizong was first appointed investigating censor of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 召為戶科給事中。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as supervising secretary in the Revenue section.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as supervising secretary in the Revenue section.

sentences.zh: 延綏幾饑，請帑金振救。

translations.literal: When Yan-sui was nearly stricken with famine, he requested treasury funds for relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan-sui was on the verge of famine, he requested treasury funds for relief.

sentences.zh: 終遼東苑馬寺卿。

translations.literal: He ended his career as director of the Stud Farm in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually served as director of the Stud Farm in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 祿以行人司擢戶科給事。

translations.literal: Lu, from the Courier Office, was promoted to supervising secretary in the Revenue section.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lu, from the Courier Office, was promoted to supervising secretary in the Revenue section.

sentences.zh: 謫後，自免歸。

translations.literal: After demotion he resigned on his own and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After his demotion he resigned and returned home.

sentences.zh: 王宗茂，字時育，京山人。

translations.literal: Wang Zongmao, courtesy name Shiyu, was a native of Jingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongmao, styled Shiyu, was a native of Jingshan.

sentences.zh: 父橋，廣東布政使。

translations.literal: His father Qiao was provincial administration commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qiao had served as provincial administration commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 從父格，太仆卿。

translations.literal: His father's younger cousin Ge was minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: His father's cousin Ge had served as minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 宗茂登嘉靖二十六年進士，授行人。

translations.literal: Zongmao passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing and was appointed courier.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongmao received his jinshi degree in the twenty-sixth year of the Jiajing reign and was appointed a courier.

sentences.zh: 三十一年擢南京御史。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was promoted to censor at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he was promoted to censor at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 時先後劾嚴嵩者皆得禍，沈煉至謫佃保安。

translations.literal: At the time those who had impeached Yan Song one after another all met with disaster; Shen Lian was even demoted to farm land at Bao'an.
translations.idiomatic: By then everyone who had impeached Yan Song in succession had met with disaster; Shen Lian had even been demoted to farm land at Bao'an.

sentences.zh: 中外懾其威，益箝口。

translations.literal: Within and without the court they feared his power and clammed up all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Within and without the court men feared his power and clammed up all the more.

sentences.zh: 宗茂積不平，甫拜官三月，上疏曰：

translations.literal: Zongmao had long nursed indignation; scarcely three months after taking office he submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongmao had long nursed his outrage; only three months after taking office he submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 嵩本邪諂之徒，寡廉鮮恥。

translations.literal: Song by nature is a wicked flatterer, bereft of integrity and shame.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song is by nature a wicked flatterer, bereft of integrity and shame.

sentences.zh: 久持國柄，作福作威。

translations.literal: Long holding the reins of state, he dispenses blessings and wields terror.
translations.idiomatic: He has long held the reins of state, dispensing favors and wielding terror.

sentences.zh: 薄海內外，罔不怨恨。

translations.literal: From the edges of the sea to the farthest reaches, none do not resent him.
translations.idiomatic: From the coasts to the hinterland, none do not resent him.

sentences.zh: 如吏、兵二部每選，請屬二十人，人索賄數百金，任自擇善地。

translations.literal: For example, at each selection by the Ministries of Officials and War, he receives requests on behalf of twenty men; each man demands several hundred in gold in bribes and may choose good posts for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Ministries of Officials and War hold selections, he accepts solicitations on behalf of twenty men at a time; each pays several hundred in gold in bribes and may choose his own desirable post.

sentences.zh: 致文武將吏盡出其門。

translations.literal: The result is that civil and military officers and functionaries all issue from his gate.
translations.idiomatic: The result is that civil and military officers all issue from his gate.

sentences.zh: 此嵩負國之罪一也。

translations.literal: This is Song's first crime against the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first of Yan Song's crimes against the state.

sentences.zh: 任私人萬寀為考功郎。

translations.literal: He installed his private retainer Wan Cai as bureau director of evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: He installed his own man Wan Cai as bureau director of evaluations.

sentences.zh: 凡外官遷擢，不察其行能，不計其資歷，唯賄是問。

translations.literal: For all transfers and promotions of outside officials, he does not examine their conduct and ability, does not consider their seniority—only bribes are asked.
translations.idiomatic: For all transfers and promotions of local officials, he does not examine conduct or ability, does not weigh seniority—only bribes matter.

sentences.zh: 致端方之士不得為國家用。

translations.literal: The result is that upright men cannot be employed by the state.
translations.idiomatic: The result is that upright men cannot serve the state.

sentences.zh: 此嵩負國之罪二也。

translations.literal: This is Song's second crime against the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second of Yan Song's crimes against the state.

sentences.zh: 往歲遭人論劾，潛輸家資南返，輦載珍寶，不可數計。

translations.literal: In past years when others denounced him, he secretly sent his household wealth back south; carriage loads of treasures were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In past years, when others denounced him, he secretly shipped his household wealth back south in carriage loads of treasure beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 金銀人物，多高二三尺者。

translations.literal: Gold and silver figurines, many of them two or three feet high.
translations.idiomatic: There were gold and silver figurines, many of them two or three feet tall.

sentences.zh: 下至溺器，亦金銀為之。

translations.literal: Down even to chamber pots, all were made of gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: Even chamber pots were made of gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 不知陛下宮中亦有此器否耶？

translations.literal: I do not know whether Your Majesty's palace also has such vessels or not?
translations.idiomatic: Does Your Majesty's palace also have such vessels?

sentences.zh: 此嵩負國之罪三也。

translations.literal: This is Song's third crime against the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third of Yan Song's crimes against the state.

sentences.zh: 廣布良田，遍於江西數郡。

translations.literal: He widely planted fine fields, spread across several prefectures of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He acquired vast tracts of fertile land spread across several prefectures in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 又於府第之後積石為大坎，實以金銀珍玩，為子孫百世計。

translations.literal: Moreover behind his mansion he piled stones into a great pit and filled it with gold, silver, and precious playthings, planning for his descendants for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Behind his mansion he piled stones into a great vault and filled it with gold, silver, and precious treasures, providing for his descendants for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 而國計民瘼，一不措懷。

translations.literal: Yet state planning and the people's suffering he does not attend to in the least.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he gives not a thought to state finances or the people's suffering.

sentences.zh: 此嵩負國之罪四也。

translations.literal: This is Song's fourth crime against the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth of Yan Song's crimes against the state.

sentences.zh: 畜家奴五百余人，往來京邸。

translations.literal: He keeps more than five hundred household slaves coming and going at his Beijing residence.
translations.idiomatic: He keeps more than five hundred household slaves coming and going at his residence in the capital.

sentences.zh: 所至騷擾驛傳，虐害居民，長吏皆怨怒而不敢言。

translations.literal: Wherever they go they harass relay stations, cruelly harm residents; local officials all resent and rage but dare not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever they go they harass relay stations and cruelly harm local residents; local officials seethe with resentment but dare not speak out.

sentences.zh: 此嵩負國之罪五也。

translations.literal: This is Song's fifth crime against the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth of Yan Song's crimes against the state.

sentences.zh: 陛下所食大官之饌不數品，而嵩則窮極珍錯。

translations.literal: Your Majesty eats from the Grand Provisioner's table only a few kinds of dish, yet Song exhausts every rare delicacy.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's table sees only a few kinds of dish from the Grand Provisioner, yet Yan Song exhausts every rare delicacy.

sentences.zh: 殊方異產，莫不畢致。

translations.literal: Exotic products from distant regions, none are not all procured.
translations.idiomatic: Exotic products from every distant region are all brought before him.

sentences.zh: 是九州萬國之待嵩有甚於陛下。

translations.literal: Thus the nine regions and myriad lands treat Song with greater attention than Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The riches of the realm are lavished on Yan Song more generously than on Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 此嵩負國之罪六也。

translations.literal: This is Song's sixth crime against the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sixth of Yan Song's crimes against the state.

sentences.zh: 往歲寇迫京畿，正上下憂懼之日，而嵩貪肆益甚。

translations.literal: In past years when bandits pressed the capital region, precisely when high and low were anxious and fearful, Song's greed and license grew all the fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders threatened the capital region last year—the very moment when court and country were gripped with fear—Yan Song's greed and license grew fiercer still.

sentences.zh: 致民俗歌謠，遍於京師，達於沙漠。

translations.literal: The result was that popular songs and ballads spread throughout the capital and reached the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Popular songs and ballads spread throughout the capital and even reached the desert frontier.

sentences.zh: 海內百姓，莫不祝天以冀其早亡，嵩尚恬不知止。

translations.literal: Among the common people throughout the realm, none did not pray Heaven hoping for his early death, yet Song still complacently does not know when to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the realm the common people prayed to Heaven for his early death, yet Yan Song still complacently knew no restraint.

sentences.zh: 此嵩負國之罪七也。

translations.literal: This is Song's seventh crime against the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is the seventh of Yan Song's crimes against the state.

sentences.zh: 募朝士為幹兒義子至三十余輩。

translations.literal: He recruited more than thirty court officials as sworn sons and adoptive sons.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited more than thirty court officials as sworn sons and adoptive sons.

sentences.zh: 若尹耕、梁紹儒，早已敗露。

translations.literal: Such as Yin Geng and Liang Shaoru—their scandals had long been exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Yin Geng and Liang Shaoru had long since been exposed.

sentences.zh: 此輩實衣冠之盜，而皆為之爪牙，助其虐焰，致朝廷恩威不出於陛下。

translations.literal: These men are truly brigands in official robes, yet all serve as his claws and fangs, helping his tyrannical blaze, so that the court's grace and authority do not issue from Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: These men are brigands in official robes, yet all serve as his claws and fangs, fueling his tyranny so that the court's grace and authority no longer flow from Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 此嵩負國之罪八也。

translations.literal: This is Song's eighth crime against the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is the eighth of Yan Song's crimes against the state.

sentences.zh: 夫天下之所恃以為安者，財也，兵也。

translations.literal: Now what the realm relies on for security is wealth and armies.
translations.idiomatic: What the realm relies on for its security is wealth and armed force.

sentences.zh: 不才之文吏，以賂而出其門，則必剝民之財，去百而求千，去千而求萬，民奈何不困？

translations.literal: If incompetent civil officials emerge from his gate through bribes, they will necessarily strip the people's wealth—seeking a thousand from a hundred, ten thousand from a thousand; how can the people not be distressed?
translations.idiomatic: When incompetent civil officials buy their way out of his gate, they inevitably strip the people—turning hundreds into thousands and thousands into ten thousands; how can the people not be ground down?

sentences.zh: 不才之武將以賂而出其門，則必克軍之餉，或缺伍而不補，或逾期而不發，兵奈何不疲？

translations.literal: If incompetent military commanders emerge from his gate through bribes, they will necessarily withhold army provisions—or leave vacancies unfilled, or issue pay overdue; how can the armies not be exhausted?
translations.idiomatic: When incompetent military commanders buy their way out of his gate, they inevitably skim army pay—leaving vacancies unfilled or issuing pay overdue; how can the troops not be worn down?

sentences.zh: 邇者，四方地震，其占為臣下專權。

translations.literal: Recently earthquakes have struck in all directions; the omen reads as ministers monopolizing authority.
translations.idiomatic: Recently earthquakes have struck throughout the realm; the omen signifies ministers monopolizing authority.

sentences.zh: 試問今日之專權者，寧有出於嵩右乎？

translations.literal: I ask: among those who monopolize authority today, could any surpass Song?
translations.idiomatic: I ask: among those who monopolize authority today, can any surpass Yan Song?

sentences.zh: 陛下之帑藏不足支諸邊一年之費，而嵩所蓄積可贍儲數年。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's treasury cannot cover the border expenses for one year, yet what Song has amassed could supply the stores for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's treasury cannot cover a single year's border expenses, yet what Yan Song has amassed could fill the stores for several years.

sentences.zh: 與其開賣官鬻爵之令以助邊，盍去此蠹國害民之賊，籍其家以紓患也？

translations.literal: Rather than issue orders to sell offices and ranks to aid the borders, why not remove this pest who harms state and people, confiscate his household to relieve the disaster?
