translations.idiomatic: Rather than issuing orders to sell offices and ranks to fund the borders, why not remove this pest who plagues state and people, and confiscate his household to relieve the crisis?

sentences.zh: 臣見數年以來，凡論嵩者不死於廷杖，則役於邊塞。

translations.literal: Your servant has seen these several years that all who denounced Song either died at court beating or labored on the border frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years I have seen that everyone who denounced Yan Song either died under the court rod or was sent to labor on the border frontiers.

sentences.zh: 臣亦有身家，寧不致惜，而敢犯九重之怒，攖權相之鋒哉？

translations.literal: Your servant too has family and self—is he not mindful of preserving them? Yet how dare he provoke the rage of the Ninefold Gates and touch the sharp edge of the power-holding minister?
translations.idiomatic: I too have a family and a life of my own—would I not cherish them? Yet how could I dare provoke the emperor's wrath and run against the power-holding chief minister?

sentences.zh: 誠念世受國恩，不忍見祖宗天下壞於賊嵩之手也。

translations.literal: Truly remembering that generation after generation he has received the state's grace, he cannot bear to see the ancestral realm ruined at the hands of the robber Song.
translations.idiomatic: It is only because I have received the state's grace life after life that I cannot bear to see the realm our ancestors built ruined in the hands of the robber Yan Song.

sentences.zh: 疏至，通政司趙文華密以示嵩，留數日始上，由是嵩得預為地。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, Zhao Wenhua of the Office of Transmission secretly showed it to Song, kept it several days before submitting it, and thereby Song was able to prepare ground in advance.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Zhao Wenhua of the Office of Transmission secretly showed it to Yan Song and held it back for several days before submitting it, thereby giving Song time to prepare his defense.

sentences.zh: 遂以誣詆大臣，謫平陽縣丞。

translations.literal: Thereupon on the charge of slandering a great minister, he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Pingyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was then demoted to assistant magistrate of Pingyang County on the charge of slandering a great minister.

sentences.zh: 方宗茂上疏，自謂必死。

translations.literal: When Zongmao submitted his memorial, he said to himself he would surely die.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zongmao submitted his memorial, he expected to die for it.

sentences.zh: 及得貶，恬然出都。

translations.literal: When he received demotion instead, he calmly left the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When he was merely demoted instead, he left the capital without distress.

sentences.zh: 到官半歲，以母憂歸。

translations.literal: Half a year after arriving at his post, he returned home on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Half a year after taking up his post, he returned home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 嵩無以釋憾，奪其父橋官。

translations.literal: Song had no way to release his grudge and stripped his father Qiao of office.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to vent his grudge, Yan Song stripped Wang Zongmao's father Qiao of his office.

sentences.zh: 橋竟憤悒卒。

translations.literal: Qiao in the end died of indignant brooding.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao ultimately died of grief and resentment.

sentences.zh: 嵩罷相之日，宗茂亦卒。

translations.literal: On the day Song was dismissed from the chief ministership, Zongmao also died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yan Song was dismissed from office, Wang Zongmao died as well.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign, he was posthumously granted the title of vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 周冕，資縣人。

translations.literal: Zhou Mian was a native of Zixian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Mian was a native of Zixian.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十年進士。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twentieth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授太常博士，擢貴州道試御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and promoted to probationary censor on the Guizhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed an erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and promoted to probationary censor on the Guizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 重建太廟成，奉安神主，帝將遣官代祭。

translations.literal: When reconstruction of the Great Temple was completed and the spirit tablets were installed, the emperor was about to dispatch officials to sacrifice in his place.
translations.idiomatic: When reconstruction of the Great Temple was completed and the spirit tablets were installed, the emperor was about to dispatch officials to sacrifice in his stead.

sentences.zh: 御史鄢懋卿言其不可。

translations.literal: Censor Yan Maoqing said this was impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yan Maoqing argued that this was impermissible.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，降手詔數百言諭廷臣，且言更有協君取譽者，必罪不宥。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry, issued a handwritten edict of several hundred words instructing the court officials, and further said that anyone who again colluded with the ruler to win praise would be punished without mercy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and issued a handwritten edict of several hundred words instructing the court officials, declaring that anyone who again colluded with the ruler to win praise would be punished without mercy.

sentences.zh: 舉朝悚息，無敢復言，冕獨抗章爭之。

translations.literal: The entire court trembled in fear and none dared speak again; Mian alone submitted a memorial in protest.
translations.idiomatic: The entire court trembled in fear and none dared speak again, but Zhou Mian alone submitted a memorial in protest.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，立下冕詔獄搒掠。

translations.literal: The emperor was profoundly enraged and immediately had Mian thrown into the imperial prison and beaten.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was profoundly enraged and immediately had Zhou Mian thrown into the imperial prison and beaten.

sentences.zh: 終以其言直，釋還職。

translations.literal: In the end, because his words were upright, he was released and restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, because his words were upright, he was released and restored to office.

sentences.zh: 是時太子生十一年矣，猶未出閣講學。

translations.literal: At that time the crown prince had already lived eleven years, yet still had not left the palace to receive lecturing instruction.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the crown prince had already lived eleven years, yet still had not left the palace to receive formal instruction.

sentences.zh: 冕極言教諭不可緩，請早降綸言，慎選侍從。

translations.literal: Mian urgently argued that princely instruction could not be delayed, and asked that an edict be issued early and attendants carefully chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Mian urgently argued that the crown prince's education could not be delayed, and asked that an edict be issued promptly and attendants be chosen with care.

sentences.zh: 帝又大怒，謫雲南通海縣典史。

translations.literal: The emperor again grew greatly angry and demoted him to clerk of Tonghai County in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again flew into a rage and demoted him to clerk of Tonghai County in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 冕雖遠竄，意慷慨無所屈。

translations.literal: Though Mian had been exiled far away, his spirit remained unbowed and uncompromising.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhou Mian had been exiled far from court, his spirit remained unbowed and uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 數遷至武選郎中。

translations.literal: After several transfers he reached director in the Bureau of Military Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: After several promotions he rose to director in the Bureau of Military Appointments.

sentences.zh: 楊繼盛劾嚴嵩及嚴效忠冒功事，語侵歐陽必進。

translations.literal: Yang Jisheng impeached Yan Song and Yan Xiaozhong's usurpation of merit, with language that encroached on Ouyang Bijin.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jisheng impeached Yan Song over Yan Xiaozhong's fraudulent claim to merit, with language that also implicated Ouyang Bijin.

sentences.zh: 必進奏辯，章下兵部。

translations.literal: Bijin submitted a defense memorial, and the memorial was sent down to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Bijin submitted a defense memorial, and the memorial was sent down to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 冕上言：

translations.literal: Mian submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Mian submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 臣奉詔檢得二十七年通政司狀，效忠年十六，因武會試未第，咨兩廣軍門聽用。

translations.literal: Your servant, pursuant to the edict, examined the petition of the Office of Transmission from the twenty-seventh year and found Xiaozhong was sixteen years old; because he had failed the military metropolitan examination, he inquired to the military gate of the two Guang for employment.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuant to the edict, I examined the petition of the Office of Transmission from the twenty-seventh year and found that Xiaozhong was sixteen years old; because he had failed the military metropolitan examination, he applied to the military command of the two Guang for employment.

sentences.zh: 已而必進及總兵官陳圭奏黎賊平，遣效忠報捷，授錦衣試所鎮撫。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Bijin together with regional commander Chen Gui memorialized that the Li bandits had been pacified, sent Xiaozhong to report victory, and he was granted trial assistant commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter Ouyang Bijin together with regional commander Chen Gui memorialized that the Li bandits had been pacified, sent Xiaozhong to report the victory, and had him granted the post of trial assistant commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 未逾月，嚴鵠言兄效忠曾斬首七級，並功加賞，應得署副千戶。

translations.literal: Not a month later, Yan Hu said his elder brother Xiaozhong had once beheaded seven ranks and that the combined merit merited additional reward, entitling him to acting deputy company commander.
translations.idiomatic: Not a month later, Yan Hu reported that his elder brother Xiaozhong had once beheaded seven enemy heads and that the combined merit merited additional reward, entitling him to acting deputy company commander.

sentences.zh: 今效忠身抱痼疾，鵠請代職。

translations.literal: Now Xiaozhong suffers from chronic illness; Hu asked to take over the post in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Now Xiaozhong suffered from chronic illness, and Hu asked to take over the post in his stead.

sentences.zh: 臣心疑其偽，方將核實以聞。

translations.literal: Your servant suspected fraud and was about to verify the facts before reporting.
translations.idiomatic: I suspected fraud and was about to verify the facts before reporting.

sentences.zh: 嵩子世蕃乃自創一槁付臣，屬臣依違題覆。

translations.literal: Song's son Shifan then drafted a document himself and gave it to your servant, instructing him to reply evasively and perfunctorily.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song's son Shifan then drafted a document himself and gave it to me, instructing me to reply evasively and perfunctorily.

sentences.zh: 臣觀其槁，率誕謾舛戾，請得一一折之。

translations.literal: Your servant examined the draft and found it full of absurd, mendacious, and contradictory errors; he asks leave to refute each one.
translations.idiomatic: I examined the draft and found it full of absurd, mendacious, and contradictory claims; I ask leave to refute each one.

sentences.zh: 如效忠曾中武舉，何初無本籍起送文牒，今又稱民人，而不言武舉？

translations.literal: If Xiaozhong had once passed the military provincial examination, why was there at first no native-place dispatch document—and now he is called a commoner without mention of the military provincial degree?
translations.idiomatic: If Xiaozhong had once passed the military provincial examination, why was there at first no native-place dispatch document—and why is he now called a commoner with no mention of that degree?

sentences.zh: 如效忠果鵠之兄，世蕃之子，則世蕃數子俱幼，未有名效忠者。

translations.literal: If Xiaozhong were truly Hu's elder brother and Shifan's son, then of Shifan's several sons all were young and none was named Xiaozhong.
translations.idiomatic: If Xiaozhong were truly Hu's elder brother and Shifan's son, then of Shifan's several sons all were still young, and none was named Xiaozhong.

sentences.zh: 如效忠果斬首七級，則當時狀稱年止十六，豈能赴戰？

translations.literal: If Xiaozhong truly beheaded seven ranks, the petition at the time said he was only sixteen—how could he go to battle?
translations.idiomatic: If Xiaozhong truly beheaded seven enemy heads, the petition at the time said he was only sixteen—how could he have gone into battle?

sentences.zh: 何軍門諸將俱未聞斬獲功，獨宰相一孫乃驍勇冠三軍？

translations.literal: Why did none of the generals at the military gate hear of merit from beheaded captures, yet the chief minister's lone grandson was bravest in all the army?
translations.idiomatic: Why did none of the generals at the military command report merit from beheaded captures, yet the chief minister's lone grandson alone was said to be the bravest in all the army?

sentences.zh: 如曰效忠對敵，脛臂受創，計臨陣及差委，相去未一月，何以萬里軍情即能馳報？

translations.literal: If it is said Xiaozhong faced the enemy and his shins and arms received wounds—counting time on campaign and dispatch, not a month had passed; how could news of military conditions ten thousand li away be reported so swiftly?
translations.idiomatic: If it is said Xiaozhong faced the enemy and his shins and arms were wounded—counting time on campaign and time in dispatch, less than a month had passed; how could news of military conditions a thousand miles away have been reported so swiftly?

sentences.zh: 如曰效忠到京以創甚疾故，何以鵠代職之日，止告不能受職？

translations.literal: If it is said Xiaozhong came to the capital because his wounds were severely ill—why on the day Hu replaced him in office did he only report inability to accept the post?
translations.idiomatic: If it is said Xiaozhong came to the capital because his wounds had grown severely ill—why on the day Hu replaced him in office did he report only that he was unable to accept the post?

sentences.zh: 如曰效忠鎮撫當代，則奏捷功止及身，例無傳襲。

translations.literal: If it is said Xiaozhong's assistant commander's post should be succeeded—merit reported in victory pertained only to the person himself; by precedent there was no transmission by inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: If it is said Xiaozhong's assistant commander's post should be succeeded—merit reported in victory pertained only to the person himself, and by precedent there was no transmission by inheritance.

sentences.zh: 如曰效忠功當並論，例先奏請，何止用通狀，而逼令司官奉行？

translations.literal: If it is said Xiaozhong's merit should be discussed together—by precedent one must first memorialize and request; why use only the transmission petition and force the responsible officials to comply?
translations.idiomatic: If it is said Xiaozhong's merit should be considered together—by precedent one must first memorialize and request approval; why use only the transmission petition and force the responsible officials to comply?

sentences.zh: 臣悉心廉訪，初未有名效忠者赴軍門聽用，鵠亦非效忠親弟。

translations.literal: Your servant thoroughly investigated in good faith; at first there was no person named Xiaozhong who went to the military gate for employment, and Hu was not Xiaozhong's younger brother by blood.
translations.idiomatic: After a thorough investigation in good faith, I found that at first no person named Xiaozhong had gone to the military command for employment, and Hu was not Xiaozhong's younger brother by blood.

sentences.zh: 其姓名乃詭設，首級亦要買，而非有纖毫實跡也。

translations.literal: The name was fraudulently invented and the head-counts were bought—there was not the slightest trace of reality.
translations.idiomatic: The name was fraudulently invented and the head-counts were purchased—there was not the slightest trace of reality.

sentences.zh: 必進既嵩鄉曲，圭又世蕃姻親，依阿朋比，共為欺罔。

translations.literal: Bijin was Song's fellow townsman and Gui was Shifan's marriage kinsman; they fawned and banded together in mutual collusion to deceive.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Bijin was Yan Song's fellow townsman and Chen Gui was Yan Shifan's marriage kinsman; they fawned on one another and colluded together in deception.

sentences.zh: 臣如不言，陛下何從知其奸？

translations.literal: If your servant did not speak, how would Your Majesty know his treachery?
translations.idiomatic: If I did not speak, how would Your Majesty know of his treachery?

sentences.zh: 且自累朝以來，未聞有宰相之子孫送軍門報效者。

translations.literal: Moreover, since successive dynasties, none has heard of a chief minister's sons and grandsons sent to the military gate to report for merit service.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since successive dynasties, none has heard of a chief minister's sons and grandsons being sent to the military command to report for merit service.

sentences.zh: 今嵩不唯咨送軍門，而且詭托名姓，破壞祖宗之制，彼蔣應奎、唐國相輩何怪其效尤耶？

translations.literal: Now Song not only inquired and sent men to the military gate, but also fraudulently borrowed names, destroying the institutions of the ancestors—should Jiang Yingkui, Tang Guoxiang, and their like be blamed for following his example?
translations.idiomatic: Now Yan Song not only inquired and sent men to the military command, but also fraudulently borrowed names and destroyed the institutions of our ancestors—why should Jiang Yingkui, Tang Guoxiang, and men like them be blamed for following his example?

sentences.zh: 臣職守攸關，義不敢隱，乞特賜究正，使天下曉然知朝廷有不可幸之功、不可犯之法。

translations.literal: Your servant's duty is intimately involved and in righteousness he dare not conceal; he humbly asks special permission to investigate and correct, so all under Heaven clearly know the court has merit that cannot be claimed by luck and laws that cannot be violated.
translations.idiomatic: My duty is intimately involved, and in righteousness I dare not conceal this; I humbly ask that a special investigation be granted, so that all under Heaven may clearly know the court has merit that cannot be claimed by luck and laws that cannot be violated.

sentences.zh: 臣雖得罪，死無所恨。

translations.literal: Though your servant should offend and die, he would harbor no regret.
translations.idiomatic: Even if I should offend and die for it, I would harbor no regret.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，直聲震朝廷。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, his upright voice shook the court.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, his upright voice shook the court.

sentences.zh: 嵩父子大懼，力事彌縫。

translations.literal: Song father and son were greatly terrified and worked hard to patch things over.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song and his son were greatly terrified and worked hard to patch things over.

sentences.zh: 帝責冕報復，下詔獄拷訊，斥為民。

translations.literal: The emperor blamed Mian for retaliation, had him sent to the imperial prison for torture and interrogation, and dismissed him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed Zhou Mian for retaliation, had him sent to the imperial prison for torture and interrogation, and dismissed him from office.

sentences.zh: 冕既得罪，而尚書覆奏如世蕃指矣。

translations.literal: Once Mian had been punished, the minister's reply memorial followed Shifan's directions.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhou Mian had been punished, the minister's reply memorial followed Yan Shifan's directions.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，錄先朝直臣，起冕太仆少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, recording upright ministers of the previous reign, Mian was recalled as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign, when upright ministers of the previous reign were honored, Zhou Mian was recalled to serve as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，未任，卒。

translations.literal: He encountered mourning for his mother, took no appointment, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was mourning his mother, took no appointment, and died.

sentences.zh: 趙錦，字元樸，余姚人。

translations.literal: Zhao Jin, courtesy name Yuanpu, was a native of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jin, styled Yuanpu, was a native of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twenty-third year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授江陰知縣，征授南京御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Jiangyin and was summoned to serve as Nanjing censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Jiangyin and was summoned to serve as a Nanjing censor.

sentences.zh: 江洋有警，議設總兵官於鎮江。

translations.literal: When there were alarms on the rivers and seas, it was proposed to establish a regional commander at Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: When there were alarms on the rivers and seas, it was proposed to establish a regional commander at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 錦言：「小寇剽掠，不足煩重兵。

translations.literal: Jin said: "Petty bandits raiding and plundering do not warrant heavy troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jin said: "Petty bandits raiding and plundering do not warrant heavy troops.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃罷之。

translations.literal: " The emperor then abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then abolished the proposal.

sentences.zh: 已，疏言：「淮兗數百里，民多流傭，乞寬租徭，簡廷臣督有司拊循。

translations.literal: Later he submitted a memorial saying: "For several hundred li in Huai and Yan, the people mostly work as hired laborers elsewhere; I beg that rents and corvée be relaxed and court ministers be chosen to supervise the local officials in soothing and guiding them.
translations.idiomatic: Later he submitted a memorial stating: "For several hundred li across Huai and Yan, the people mostly work as hired laborers elsewhere; I beg that rents and corvée be relaxed and court ministers be chosen to supervise the local officials in soothing and guiding them.

sentences.zh: 」報可。

translations.literal: " The response was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 軍興，民輸粟馬，得官錦衣，錦極陳不可。

translations.literal: When military campaigns were launched, civilians who supplied grain and horses received Embroidered Uniform Guard appointments; Jin urgently memorialized that this was impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: When military campaigns were launched, civilians who supplied grain and horses were granted Embroidered Uniform Guard appointments; Zhao Jin urgently memorialized that this was impermissible.

sentences.zh: 尋清軍雲南。

translations.literal: Soon after he conducted a military household review in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he conducted a military household review in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 三十二年元旦，日食。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the thirty-second year, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the thirty-second year, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 錦以為權奸亂政之應，馳疏劾嚴嵩罪。

translations.literal: Jin believed this was a response to powerful traitors disturbing governance and hurriedly submitted a memorial impeaching Yan Song's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jin believed this was a response to powerful traitors disturbing governance and hurriedly submitted a memorial impeaching Yan Song's crimes.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：

translations.literal: Its summary said:
translations.idiomatic: Its summary said:

sentences.zh: 臣伏見日食元旦，變異非常。

translations.literal: Your servant observes a solar eclipse on New Year's Day—an omen surpassing the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that a solar eclipse on New Year's Day is an omen surpassing the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 又山東、徐、淮仍歲大水，四方頻地震，災不虛生。

translations.literal: Also Shandong, Xu, and Huai still suffer floods year after year, and earthquakes are frequent in all directions; calamities are not born without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Shandong, Xu, and Huai still suffer floods year after year, and earthquakes are frequent in all directions; calamities are not born without cause.

sentences.zh: 昔太祖高皇帝罷丞相，散其權於諸司，為後世慮至深遠矣。

translations.literal: Formerly Grand Ancestor Emperor Gaozu abolished the chancellor and dispersed his power among the various offices—a precaution for posterity profound and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Grand Ancestor Emperor Taizu abolished the chancellor and dispersed his power among the various offices—a precaution for posterity profound and far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 今之內閣，無宰相之名，而有其實，非高皇帝本意。

translations.literal: Today's Grand Secretariat has no chancellor's name yet holds its reality—not Grand Ancestor Gaozu's original intent.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Grand Secretariat has no chancellor's title yet holds its power—not Grand Ancestor Taizu's original intent.

sentences.zh: 頃夏言以貪暴之資，恣睢其間。

translations.literal: Recently Xia Yan with his greedy and violent nature acted with wanton arrogance in its midst.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Xia Yan, with his greedy and violent nature, acted with wanton arrogance within it.

sentences.zh: 今大學士嵩又以佞奸之雄，繼之怙寵張威，竊權縱欲，事無鉅細，罔不自專。

translations.literal: Now Grand Secretary Song again, as a villainous sycophant, succeeded him, relying on favor to expand his power, stealing authority and indulging desire—nothing great or small in which he does not act arbitrarily on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Now Grand Secretary Yan Song, a villainous sycophant, succeeded him, relying on favor to expand his power, stealing authority and indulging his desires—nothing great or small in which he does not act arbitrarily on his own.

sentences.zh: 人有違忤，必中以禍，百司望風惕息。

translations.literal: Whoever opposed him he surely struck with disaster; all departments looked to the wind and trembled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever opposed him he surely struck with disaster; all departments looked to the wind and trembled in fear.

sentences.zh: 天下事未聞朝廷，先以聞政府。

translations.literal: Affairs of the realm were not heard at court first—they were heard at the government first.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs of the realm were not heard at court first—they were heard at the Grand Secretariat first.

sentences.zh: 白事之官，班候於其門；

translations.literal: Officials presenting reports waited in ranks at its gate;
translations.idiomatic: Officials presenting reports waited in ranks at its gate;

sentences.zh: 請求之賂，幅輳於其室。

translations.literal: Requests and bribes converged in heaps at its rooms.
translations.idiomatic: Requests and bribes converged in heaps at its rooms.

sentences.zh: 銓司黜陟，本兵用舍，莫不承意指。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Appointments' dismissals and promotions, the Ministry of War's appointments and dismissals—all followed his intended directions.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Appointments' dismissals and promotions, the Ministry of War's appointments and dismissals—all followed his intended directions.

sentences.zh: 邊臣失事，率朘削軍資納賕嵩所，無功可以受賞，有罪可以逭誅。

translations.literal: Border officials who failed in duty generally skimmed military funds to offer bribes at Song's place—without merit they could receive rewards, with guilt they could escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Border officials who failed in duty generally skimmed military funds to offer bribes to Yan Song—without merit they could receive rewards, with guilt they could escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 至宗藩勛戚之襲封，文武大臣之贈謚，其遲速予奪，一視賂之厚薄。

translations.literal: Even the succession of enfeoffments for imperial clansmen and meritorious kin, and the posthumous titles of civil and military great ministers—their delay, speed, grant, or denial all depended on the thickness of bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Even the succession of enfeoffments for imperial clansmen and meritorious kin, and the posthumous titles of civil and military great ministers—their delay, speed, grant, or denial all depended on the size of bribes.

sentences.zh: 以至希寵幹進之徒，妄自貶損。

translations.literal: Even those who curried favor and schemed for advancement presumptuously debased themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Even those who curried favor and schemed for advancement presumptuously debased themselves.

sentences.zh: 稱號不倫，廉恥掃地，有臣所不忍言者。

translations.literal: Titles were irregular, shame and integrity were swept clean—there is what your servant cannot bear to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Titles were irregular, shame and integrity were swept clean—there are things I cannot bear to speak of.

sentences.zh: 陛下天縱聖神，乾綱獨運，自以予奪由宸斷，題覆在諸司，閣臣擬旨取裁而已。

translations.literal: Your Majesty heaven-endowed with sagely spirit, the great net operated alone—taking for granted that grants and denials come from imperial decision, title replies rest with the various offices, and grand secretaries merely draft edicts for approval.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is heaven-endowed with sagely spirit and holds the great net alone—taking for granted that grants and denials come from Your Majesty's decision, title replies rest with the various offices, and grand secretaries merely draft edicts for approval.

sentences.zh: 諸司奏稿，並承命於嵩，陛下安得知之？

translations.literal: Memorial drafts of the various offices all received orders from Song—how would Your Majesty know?
translations.idiomatic: Memorial drafts of the various offices all received orders from Yan Song—how would Your Majesty know?

sentences.zh: 今言誅，而嵩得播惡者，言剛暴而疏淺，惡易見，嵩柔佞而機深，惡難知也。

translations.literal: Now when speech denounces, Song can broadcast evil—Yan was fierce and rough yet shallow in his memorials, evil easy to see; Song is soft and sycophantic yet deep in scheming, evil hard to know.
translations.idiomatic: Now when speech denounces, Yan Song can broadcast evil—Xia Yan was fierce and rough yet shallow in his memorials, so his evil was easy to see; Yan Song is soft and sycophantic yet deep in scheming, so his evil is hard to know.

sentences.zh: 嵩窺伺逢迎之巧，似乎忠勤，諂諛側媚之態，似乎恭順。

translations.literal: Song watched and waited with cunning in fawning and compliance, seeming dutiful and diligent; with flattery and sidelong obsequiousness, seeming respectful and obedient.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song watched and waited with cunning in fawning and compliance, seeming dutiful and diligent; with flattery and sidelong obsequiousness, he seemed respectful and obedient.

sentences.zh: 引植私人，布列要地，伺諸臣之動靜，而先發以制之，故敗露者少。

translations.literal: He introduced and planted private men deployed at key posts, watched the movements of various ministers, and struck first to control them—therefore few were exposed.
translations.idiomatic: He introduced and planted private men at key posts, watched the movements of various ministers, and struck first to control them—therefore few were exposed.

sentences.zh: 厚賂左右親信之人，凡陛下動靜意向，無不先得，故稱旨者多。

translations.literal: He gave generous bribes to those close and trusted around Your Majesty; whatever Your Majesty's movements and intentions, none were not obtained first—therefore those who hit the mark were many.
translations.idiomatic: He gave generous bribes to those close and trusted around Your Majesty; whatever Your Majesty's movements and intentions, he learned of them first—therefore those who hit the mark were many.

sentences.zh: 或伺聖意所註，因而行之以成其私；

translations.literal: Sometimes he watched what the sacred mind favored and accordingly acted to accomplish his private ends;
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he watched what Your Majesty favored and accordingly acted to accomplish his private ends;

sentences.zh: 或乘事機所會，從而鼓之以肆其毒。

translations.literal: Sometimes he seized converging opportunities of affairs and accordingly stirred them to unleash his poison.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he seized converging opportunities and accordingly stirred them up to unleash his poison.

sentences.zh: 使陛下思之，則其端本發於朝廷；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty thought about it, their root origin sprang from court;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty thought about it, their root origin sprang from the court;

sentences.zh: 使天下指之，則其事不由於政府。

translations.literal: If all under Heaven pointed at it, the affairs did not come from the government.
translations.idiomatic: If all under Heaven pointed at it, the affairs did not come from the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 幸而洞察於聖心，則諸司代嵩受其罰；

translations.literal: Fortunately if penetrating insight arose in the sacred mind, then the various offices received Song's punishment in his stead;
translations.idiomatic: If penetrating insight arose in Your Majesty's mind, then the various offices received Yan Song's punishment in his stead;

sentences.zh: 不幸而遂傳於後世，則陛下代嵩受其愆。

translations.literal: Unluckily if it passed to later generations, then Your Majesty received Song's fault in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: If it passed to later generations, then Your Majesty would receive Yan Song's fault in his stead.

sentences.zh: 陛下豈誠以嵩為賢邪？

translations.literal: Does Your Majesty truly regard Song as worthy?
translations.idiomatic: Does Your Majesty truly regard Yan Song as worthy?

sentences.zh: 自嵩輔政以來，惟恩怨是酬，惟貨賄是斂。

translations.literal: Since Song assisted in governance, only gratitude and resentment were requited, only goods and bribes were gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yan Song assisted in governance, only gratitude and resentment have been requited, only goods and bribes have been gathered.

sentences.zh: 群臣憚陰中之禍，而忠言不敢直陳；

translations.literal: Various ministers feared the disaster of secret strikes, and upright words dared not be spoken plainly;
translations.idiomatic: Various ministers feared the disaster of secret strikes, and upright words dared not be spoken plainly;

sentences.zh: 四方習貪墨之風，而閭閻日以愁困。

translations.literal: All directions learned the wind of corruption, and lanes and hamlets daily grew distressed and impoverished.
translations.idiomatic: All directions learned the wind of corruption, and lanes and hamlets daily grew distressed and impoverished.

sentences.zh: 頃自庚戌之後，外寇陸梁。

translations.literal: Recently since after gengxu, outer enemies rampaged.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, since the gengxu year, foreign enemies have rampaged.

sentences.zh: 陛下嘗募天下之武勇以足兵，竭天下之財力以給餉，搜天下之遺逸以任將，行不次之賞，施莫測之威，以風示內外矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty once recruited the realm's martial valor to fill the army, exhausted the realm's financial power to supply rations, searched the realm's hidden talents to appoint generals, applied unprecedented rewards, exerted unfathomable authority—to display awe inward and outward.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty once recruited the realm's martial valor to fill the army, exhausted the realm's financial power to supply rations, searched the realm's hidden talents to appoint generals, applied unprecedented rewards, and exerted unfathomable authority—to display awe inward and outward.

sentences.zh: 而封疆之臣卒未有為陛下寬宵旰憂者。

translations.literal: Yet border officials in the end had none who relieved Your Majesty's anxiety at dawn and dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Yet among the border officials, in the end none has relieved Your Majesty's anxiety at dawn and dusk.

sentences.zh: 蓋緣權臣行私，將吏風靡，以掊克為務，以營競為能。

translations.literal: This is because the power-holding minister acted privately and generals and officials followed the wind, taking squeezing as their task and scheming competition as their ability.
translations.idiomatic: This is because the power-holding minister acted privately and generals and officials followed the wind, taking squeezing as their task and scheming competition as their ability.

sentences.zh: 致朝廷之上，用者不賢，賢者不用；

translations.literal: On the court above, those employed were not worthy, those worthy were not employed;
translations.idiomatic: At court, those employed were not worthy, and those worthy were not employed;

sentences.zh: 賞不當功，罰不當罪。

translations.literal: Rewards did not match merit, punishments did not match crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards did not match merit, and punishments did not match crimes.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲致太平，則群臣不足承德於左右；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty wished to attain Great Peace, then the various ministers were insufficient to receive and carry virtue at left and right;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty wishes to attain Great Peace, then the various ministers are insufficient to receive and carry virtue at Your side;

sentences.zh: 欲遏戎寇，則將士不足禦侮於邊疆。

translations.literal: If he wished to check foreign enemies, then officers and soldiers were insufficient to repel insult at the borders.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty wishes to check foreign enemies, then officers and soldiers are insufficient to repel insult at the borders.

sentences.zh: 財用已竭，而外患未見底寧；

translations.literal: Financial resources were already exhausted, yet external troubles had not seen bottom peace;
translations.idiomatic: Financial resources are already exhausted, yet external troubles have not seen lasting peace;

sentences.zh: 民困已極，而內變又虞將作。

translations.literal: The people's distress had already reached its extreme, yet internal turmoil was likewise feared soon to arise.
translations.idiomatic: The people's distress has already reached its extreme, yet internal turmoil is likewise feared soon to arise.

sentences.zh: 陛下躬秉至聖，憂勤萬幾，三十二年於茲矣，而天下之勢其危如此，非嵩之奸邪，何以致之？

translations.literal: Your Majesty personally holds supreme sagacity, worrying over and laboring at myriad affairs—for thirty-two years to this day—yet the realm's situation is so perilous; if not Song's treachery and wickedness, what could have brought it about?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty personally holds supreme sagacity, worrying over and laboring at myriad affairs—for thirty-two years to this day—yet the realm's situation is so perilous; if not Yan Song's treachery and wickedness, what could have brought it about?

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下觀上天垂象，察祖宗立法之微，念權柄之不可使移，思紀綱之不可使亂，立斥罷嵩，以應天變，則朝廷清明，法紀振飭。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to observe Heaven's displayed omens, scrutinize the subtleties of the ancestral founders' lawmaking, reflect that authority cannot be allowed to shift, consider that institutions and norms cannot be allowed to fall into disorder, immediately dismiss and remove Song to respond to Heaven's changes—then the court will be clear and bright, law and discipline will be restored and ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to observe Heaven's displayed omens, scrutinize the subtleties of the ancestral founders' lawmaking, reflect that authority cannot be allowed to shift, consider that institutions and norms cannot be allowed to fall into disorder, immediately dismiss Yan Song to respond to Heaven's warning—then the court will be clear and bright, and law and discipline will be restored.

sentences.zh: 寇戎雖橫，臣知其不足平矣。

translations.literal: Though bandits and barbarians run rampant, your servant knows they are not difficult to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Though bandits and barbarians run rampant, I know they will not be difficult to pacify.

sentences.zh: 當是時，楊繼盛以劾嵩得重譴，帝方蓄怒以待言者。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Jisheng had received severe punishment for impeaching Song; the emperor was just then storing anger waiting for memorialists.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yang Jisheng had received severe punishment for impeaching Yan Song; the emperor was just then storing anger waiting for memorialists.

sentences.zh: 周冕爭冒功事亦下獄，而錦疏適至。

translations.literal: Zhou Mian's dispute over fraudulent merit claims also had him sent to prison, and Jin's memorial happened to arrive just then.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Mian's dispute over fraudulent merit claims also had him sent to prison, and Zhao Jin's memorial happened to arrive just then.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，手批其上，謂錦欺天謗君，遣使逮治，復慰諭嵩備至。

translations.literal: The emperor was shaken with rage, wrote comments in his own hand on it, saying Jin had deceived Heaven and slandered the ruler; he sent envoys to arrest and punish him, and again comforted and instructed Song most thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was shaken with rage, wrote comments in his own hand on it, saying Zhao Jin had deceived Heaven and slandered the ruler; he sent envoys to arrest and punish him, and again comforted and instructed Yan Song most thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 於是錦萬里就征，屢墮檻車，瀕死者數矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jin travelled ten thousand li to answer the summons, repeatedly fell from the prisoner cart, and several times came near death.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Zhao Jin travelled ten thousand li to answer the summons, repeatedly fell from the prisoner cart, and several times came near death.

sentences.zh: 既至，下詔獄拷訊，搒四十，斥為民。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he was sent to the imperial prison for torture and interrogation, beaten forty strokes, and dismissed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, he was sent to the imperial prison for torture and interrogation, beaten forty strokes, and dismissed to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 父塤，時為廣西參議，亦投劾罷。

translations.literal: His father Kun, then serving as Guangxi participation secretary, also submitted a memorial of resignation and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kun, then serving as Guangxi participation secretary, also submitted a resignation memorial and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 錦家居十五年，穆宗即位，起故官。

translations.literal: Jin lived at home fifteen years; when Muzong succeeded to the throne, he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jin lived at home fifteen years; when Emperor Muzong succeeded to the throne, he was restored to his former office.

sentences.zh: 擢太常少卿，未上，進光祿卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; before taking office, he was further promoted to Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; before taking office, he was further promoted to Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 江陰歲進子鱭萬斤，奏減其半。

translations.literal: Jiangyin annually submitted ten thousand jin of young hairtail; he memorialized to reduce this by half.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangyin annually submitted ten thousand jin of young hairtail; he memorialized to reduce this by half.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年以右副都御史巡撫貴州，破擒叛苗龍得鲊等。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing he served as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief governing Guizhou, defeating and capturing the rebellious Miao Long Dezha and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longqing he served as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief governing Guizhou, defeating and capturing the rebellious Miao Long Dezha and others.

sentences.zh: 宣慰安氏素桀驁，畏錦，為效命。

translations.literal: The Pacification Superintendent An clan had always been fierce and unruly; they feared Jin and rendered service.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacification Superintendent An clan had always been fierce and unruly; they feared Zhao Jin and rendered service.

sentences.zh: 入為大理卿，歷工部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Minister of Punishments, and successively served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Minister of Punishments, and successively served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 嘗署部事，有所爭執。

translations.literal: Once when he temporarily handled ministry affairs, there was some dispute.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he temporarily handled ministry affairs, there was some dispute.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二年，遷南京右都御史，改刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wanli he was transferred to Right Censor-in-Chief of Nanjing and then changed to Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wanli he was transferred to Right Censor-in-Chief of Nanjing and then changed to Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 張居正遭喪，南京大臣議疏留。

translations.literal: When Zhang Juzheng encountered bereavement, the grand ministers at Nanjing discussed submitting a memorial to retain him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng encountered bereavement, the grand ministers at Nanjing discussed submitting a memorial to retain him.

sentences.zh: 錦及工部尚書費三旸不可而止。

translations.literal: Jin and Minister of Works Fei Sanyang said it could not be done, and the plan stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jin and Minister of Works Fei Sanyang said it could not be done, and the plan stopped.

sentences.zh: 移禮部，又移吏部，俱在南京。

translations.literal: He moved to the Ministry of Rites, then again to the Ministry of Personnel, both at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to the Ministry of Rites, then again to the Ministry of Personnel, both at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 錦以居正操切，頗訾議之。

translations.literal: Jin, because Zhang Juzheng was demanding and severe, frequently criticized and discussed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jin, because Zhang Juzheng was demanding and severe, frequently criticized and discussed him.

sentences.zh: 語聞，居正令給事中費尚伊劾錦講學談禪，妄議朝政，錦遂乞休去。

translations.literal: When his words were heard, Zhang Juzheng had Supervising Secretary Fei Shangyi impeach Jin for lecturing on learning and discussing Chan, and rashly discussing court affairs; Jin thereupon requested retirement and left.
translations.idiomatic: When his words were heard, Zhang Juzheng had Supervising Secretary Fei Shangyi impeach Zhao Jin for lecturing on learning and discussing Chan, and rashly discussing court affairs; Zhao Jin thereupon requested retirement and left.

sentences.zh: 居正死，給事、御史交薦，起故官。

translations.literal: When Zhang Juzheng died, supervising secretaries and censors jointly recommended him, and he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng died, supervising secretaries and censors jointly recommended him, and he was restored to his former office.

sentences.zh: 十一年召拜左都御史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was summoned and appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was summoned and appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 是時，方籍居正貲產。

translations.literal: At that time, they were just then seizing Zhang Juzheng's property for the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, they were just then seizing Zhang Juzheng's property for the treasury.

sentences.zh: 錦言：「世宗籍嚴嵩家，禍延江西諸府。

translations.literal: Jin said: "Emperor Shizong seized Yan Song's household property, and disaster spread to the prefectures of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jin said: "Emperor Shizong seized Yan Song's household property, and disaster spread to the prefectures of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 居正私藏未必逮嚴氏，若加搜索，恐貽害三楚，十倍江西民。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng's private holdings may not reach the scale of the Yan clan; if searches are added, I fear harm will be inflicted on the Three Chu, ten times what befell the people of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng's private holdings may not reach the scale of the Yan clan; if searches are added, I fear harm will be inflicted on the Three Chu, ten times what befell the people of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 且居正誠擅權，非有異志。

translations.literal: Moreover, though Zhang Juzheng truly monopolized power, he had no divergent ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though Zhang Juzheng truly monopolized power, he had no divergent ambition.

sentences.zh: 其翊戴沖聖，夙夜勤勞，中外寧謐，功亦有不容泯者。

translations.literal: In supporting and upholding the youthful sage emperor, he toiled day and night; within and without the court were tranquil; his achievements also had aspects that cannot be extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: In supporting and upholding the youthful sage emperor, he toiled day and night; within and without the court were tranquil; his achievements also had aspects that cannot be extinguished.

sentences.zh: 今其官蔭贈謚及諸子官職並從褫革，已足示懲，乞特哀矜，稍寬其罰。

translations.literal: Now his official privileges, posthumous enfeoffment, posthumous title, and his sons' official posts have all been stripped—already sufficient to show punishment; I beg special compassion, and that the penalty be somewhat relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: Now his official privileges, posthumous enfeoffment, posthumous title, and his sons' official posts have all been stripped—already sufficient to show punishment; I beg special compassion, and that the penalty be somewhat relaxed.

sentences.zh: 」不納。

translations.literal: " [It was] not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " [It was] not adopted.

sentences.zh: 二品六年滿，加太子少保，尋加兵部尚書，掌院事如故。

translations.literal: After six years at the second rank was complete, he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; soon after he was further given Minister of War, continuing to direct the Censorate as before.
translations.idiomatic: After six years at the second rank was complete, he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; soon after he was further given Minister of War, continuing to direct the Censorate as before.

sentences.zh: 錦摘陳御史封事可采者數條，請旨行之。

translations.literal: Jin selected several items from censorial sealed memorials that were worth adopting, and requested imperial approval to implement them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jin selected several items from censorial sealed memorials that were worth adopting, and requested imperial approval to implement them.

sentences.zh: 四川巡按雒遵憾錦，假條奏指錦為奸臣。

translations.literal: Sichuan touring censor Luo Zun bore a grudge against Jin and, under pretense of a routine memorial, pointed at Jin as a treacherous minister.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan touring censor Luo Zun bore a grudge against Zhao Jin and, under pretense of a routine memorial, pointed at Zhao Jin as a treacherous minister.

sentences.zh: 御史周希旦、給事中陳與郊不直遵，交章論列，遂調遵外任。

translations.literal: Censor Zhou Xidan and Supervising Secretary Chen Yujiao did not approve of Zun; they submitted successive memorials discussing the matter, and Zun was then transferred to an outside post.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhou Xidan and Supervising Secretary Chen Yujiao did not approve of Luo Zun; they submitted successive memorials discussing the matter, and Luo Zun was then transferred to an outside post.

sentences.zh: 帝幸山陵，再奉敕居守。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited the imperial tombs, he twice received imperial orders to remain and guard [the capital].
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the imperial tombs, Zhao Jin twice received imperial orders to remain and guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 其冬，以繼母喪歸。

translations.literal: That winter he returned home on account of his stepmother's death.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he returned home on account of his stepmother's death.

sentences.zh: 十九年召拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was summoned and appointed Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was summoned and appointed Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 年七十六矣，再辭，不許。

translations.literal: He was seventy-six years old; he declined twice but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventy-six years old; he declined twice but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 次蘇州卒。

translations.literal: He died at Suzhou while en route.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Suzhou while en route.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚端肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; his posthumous title was Duansu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; his posthumous title was Duansu (Dignified and Solemn).

sentences.zh: 錦始終厲清操，篤信王守仁學，而教人則以躬行為本。

translations.literal: Jin maintained rigorous purity of conduct throughout; he deeply believed in Wang Shouren's learning, yet in teaching others he took personal conduct as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jin maintained rigorous purity of conduct throughout; he deeply believed in Wang Shouren's learning, yet in teaching others he took personal conduct as the foundation.

sentences.zh: 守仁從祀孔廟，錦有力焉。

translations.literal: When Wang Shouren was granted a place in the Confucian temple, Jin had contributed effort to it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shouren was granted a place in the Confucian temple, Zhao Jin had contributed effort to it.

sentences.zh: 始忤嚴嵩，得重禍。

translations.literal: At first he offended Yan Song and suffered severe calamity.
translations.idiomatic: At first he offended Yan Song and suffered severe calamity.

sentences.zh: 及之官貴州，道嵩裏，見嵩葬路旁，惻然憫之，屬有司護視。

translations.literal: When he went to his post in Guizhou, passing by Yan Song's native district, he saw Song buried by the roadside; moved with compassion, he instructed local officials to guard and watch over it.
translations.idiomatic: When he went to his post in Guizhou, passing by Yan Song's native district, he saw Yan Song buried by the roadside; moved with compassion, he instructed local officials to guard and watch over it.

sentences.zh: 後忤居正罷官，居正被籍，復為營救。

translations.literal: Later he offended Zhang Juzheng and was dismissed; when Juzheng's property was seized, he again worked to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he offended Zhang Juzheng and was dismissed; when Zhang Juzheng's property was seized, he again worked to rescue him.

sentences.zh: 人以是稱錦長者。

translations.literal: People for this reason called Jin a man of generous character.
translations.idiomatic: People for this reason called Zhao Jin a man of generous character.

sentences.zh: 吳時來，字惟修，仙居人。

translations.literal: Wu Shilai, courtesy name Weixiu, was a native of Xianju.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shilai, styled Weixiu, was a native of Xianju.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十二年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the thirty-second year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in the thirty-second year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 授松江推官，攝府事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Songjiang investigating magistrate and acted in prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Songjiang investigating magistrate and acted in prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 倭犯境，鄉民攜妻子趨城，時來悉納之。

translations.literal: When Japanese pirates invaded the border, villagers carrying wives and children rushed to the city; Shilai admitted them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Japanese pirates invaded the border, villagers carrying wives and children rushed to the city; Wu Shilai admitted them all.

sentences.zh: 客兵獷悍好剽掠，時來以恩結其長，犯即行法，無嘩者。

translations.literal: Guest troops were fierce and unruly and prone to plunder; Shilai won over their leaders with kindness, and when offenders violated law he immediately applied punishment—there were none who made an uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Guest troops were fierce and unruly and prone to plunder; Wu Shilai won over their leaders with kindness, and when offenders violated the law he immediately applied punishment—there were none who made an uproar.

sentences.zh: 賊攻城，驟雨，城壞數丈。

translations.literal: When bandits attacked the city, a sudden rainstorm broke several zhang of the wall.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits attacked the city, a sudden rainstorm broke several zhang of the wall.

sentences.zh: 時來以勁騎扼其沖，急興版築，三日城復完，賊乃棄去。

translations.literal: Shilai used strong cavalry to hold their assault route, urgently raised ramparts, and in three days the wall was restored; the bandits then abandoned the siege and left.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shilai used strong cavalry to hold their assault route, urgently raised ramparts, and in three days the wall was restored; the bandits then abandoned the siege and left.

sentences.zh: 擢刑科給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Supervising Secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supervising Secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 劾罷兵部尚書許論、宣大總督楊順及巡按御史路楷。

translations.literal: He impeached and had dismissed Minister of War Xu Lun, Xuan-Da grand coordinator Yang Shun, and touring censor Lu Kai.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached and had dismissed Minister of War Xu Lun, Xuan-Da grand coordinator Yang Shun, and touring censor Lu Kai.

sentences.zh: 皆嚴嵩私人，嵩疾之甚。

translations.literal: All were Yan Song's private clients; Song hated him deeply for this.
translations.idiomatic: All were Yan Song's private clients; Yan Song hated him deeply for this.

sentences.zh: 會將遣使琉球，遂以命時來。

translations.literal: It happened that envoys were about to be dispatched to Ryukyu, so the assignment was given to Shilai.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that envoys were about to be dispatched to Ryukyu, so the assignment was given to Wu Shilai.

sentences.zh: 三十七年三月，時來抗章劾嵩曰：「頃陛下赫然震怒，逮治僨事邊臣，人心莫不欣快。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirty-seventh year, Shilai submitted a defiant memorial impeaching Song, saying: "Recently Your Majesty was suddenly shaken with rage and had the border officials responsible for the failed affair arrested and punished; in people's hearts none failed to rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirty-seventh year, Wu Shilai submitted a defiant memorial impeaching Yan Song, saying: "Recently Your Majesty was suddenly shaken with rage and had the border officials responsible for the failed affair arrested and punished; in people's hearts none failed to rejoice.

sentences.zh: 邊臣朘軍實、饋執政，罪也。

translations.literal: Border officials depleted military strength and presented gifts to the chief administrator—that is a crime.
translations.idiomatic: Border officials depleted military strength and presented gifts to the chief administrator—that is a crime.

sentences.zh: 執政受其饋，朋奸罔上，獨得無罪哉？

translations.literal: The chief administrator received their gifts, colluded in wickedness and deceived the throne—can he alone be without guilt?
translations.idiomatic: The chief administrator received their gifts, colluded in wickedness and deceived the throne—can he alone be without guilt?

sentences.zh: 嵩輔政二十年，文武遷除，悉出其手。

translations.literal: Song has assisted in governance twenty years; civil and military appointments and removals all issue from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song has assisted in governance twenty years; civil and military appointments and removals all issue from his hand.

sentences.zh: 潛令子世蕃出入禁所，批答章奏。

translations.literal: He secretly had his son Shifan enter and leave the forbidden precincts to draft replies to memorials.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly had his son Yan Shifan enter and leave the forbidden precincts to draft replies to memorials.

sentences.zh: 世蕃因招權示威，頤指公卿，奴視將帥，筐篚苞苴，輻輳山積，猶無饜足。

translations.literal: Shifan therefore gathered power to display authority, commanding with a gesture the grand secretaries, treating generals as slaves; baskets of gifts piled mountain-high still did not satisfy him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shifan therefore gathered power to display authority, commanding with a gesture the grand secretaries, treating generals as slaves; baskets of gifts piled mountain-high still did not satisfy him.

sentences.zh: 用所親萬寀為文選郎，方祥為職方郎，每行一事，推一官，必先稟命世蕃而後奏請。

translations.literal: He appointed his intimates Wan Cai as Bureau of Appointments secretary and Fang Xiang as Bureau of Military Appointments secretary; for every action taken and every official promoted, he would first report to Shifan for orders and only then submit the request.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed his intimates Wan Cai as Bureau of Appointments secretary and Fang Xiang as Bureau of Military Appointments secretary; for every action taken and every official promoted, he would first report to Yan Shifan for orders and only then submit the request.

sentences.zh: 陛下但知議出部臣，豈知皆嵩父子私意哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty only knows that deliberations come from ministry officials—how could you know they are all the private intentions of Song father and son!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty only knows that deliberations come from ministry officials—how could you know they are all the private intentions of Yan Song father and son!

sentences.zh: 他不具論。

translations.literal: Other matters need not be discussed in full.
translations.idiomatic: Other matters need not be discussed in full.

sentences.zh: 如趙文華、王汝孝、張經、蔡克廉以及楊順、吳嘉會輩，或祈免死，或祈遷官，皆剝民膏以營私利，虛官帑以實權門，陛下已洞見其一二。

translations.literal: Such men as Zhao Wenhua, Wang Ruxiao, Zhang Jing, Cai Kelian, as well as Yang Shun and Wu Jiahui—some begging exemption from death, some begging transfer of office—all stripped the people's fat to pursue private gain and emptied the treasury to fill the gates of power; Your Majesty has already seen through one or two of these.
translations.idiomatic: Such men as Zhao Wenhua, Wang Ruxiao, Zhang Jing, Cai Kelian, as well as Yang Shun and Wu Jiahui—some begging exemption from death, some begging transfer of office—all stripped the people's fat to pursue private gain and emptied the treasury to fill the gates of power; Your Majesty has already seen through one or two of these.

sentences.zh: 言官如給事中袁洪愈、張墱，御史萬民英亦嘗屢及之。

translations.literal: Censorial officials such as Supervising Secretaries Yuan Hongyu and Zhang Yi, and Censor Wan Minying, have also repeatedly touched on these matters.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials such as Supervising Secretaries Yuan Hongyu and Zhang Yi, and Censor Wan Minying, have also repeatedly touched on these matters.

sentences.zh: 顧多旁指微諷，無直攻嵩父子者。

translations.literal: Yet most have indirectly pointed and subtly satirized; none have directly attacked Song father and son.
translations.idiomatic: Yet most have indirectly pointed and subtly satirized; none have directly attacked Yan Song father and son.

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂除惡務本。

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers that in removing evil one must address the root.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant privately considers that in removing evil one must address the root.

sentences.zh: 今邊事不振由於軍困，軍困由官邪，官邪由執政之好貨。

translations.literal: Now border affairs fail to revive because the army is impoverished; the army is impoverished because officials are corrupt; officials are corrupt because the chief administrator loves goods.
translations.idiomatic: Now border affairs fail to revive because the army is impoverished; the army is impoverished because officials are corrupt; officials are corrupt because the chief administrator loves goods.

sentences.zh: 若不去嵩父子，陛下雖宵旰憂勞，邊事終不可為也。」

translations.literal: If Song father and son are not removed, though Your Majesty toils at dawn and dusk with worry and labor, border affairs can never succeed."
translations.idiomatic: If Yan Song father and son are not removed, though Your Majesty toils at dawn and dusk with worry and labor, border affairs can never succeed."

sentences.zh: 時張翀、董傳策與時來同日劾嵩。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Chong and Dong Chuance impeached Song on the same day as Shilai.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Chong and Dong Chuance impeached Yan Song on the same day as Wu Shilai.

sentences.zh: 而翀及時來皆徐階門生，傳策則階邑子，時來先又官松江，於是嵩疑階主使。

translations.literal: Chong and Shilai were both Xu Jie's disciples; Chuance was a townsman of Jie's district; Shilai had previously served at Songjiang—thereupon Song suspected Jie had masterminded it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong and Wu Shilai were both Xu Jie's disciples; Dong Chuance was a townsman of Jie's district; Wu Shilai had previously served at Songjiang—thereupon Yan Song suspected Xu Jie had masterminded it.

sentences.zh: 密奏三人同日構陷，必有人主之，且時來乃憚琉球之行，借端自脫。

translations.literal: He secretly memorialized that the three on the same day had framed him, so there must have been a mastermind; moreover Shilai feared the Ryukyu mission and seized a pretext to escape it.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly memorialized that the three on the same day had framed him, so there must have been a mastermind; moreover Wu Shilai feared the Ryukyu mission and seized a pretext to escape it.

sentences.zh: 帝入其言，遂下三人詔獄，嚴鞫主謀者。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words; thereupon the three were sent to the imperial prison, and the mastermind was sternly interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his words; thereupon the three were sent to the imperial prison, and the mastermind was sternly interrogated.

sentences.zh: 三人瀕死不承，第言「此高廟神靈教臣為此言耳。

translations.literal: The three, near death, did not confess; they only said, "This was the High Temple's divine spirit teaching your servant to speak these words.
translations.idiomatic: The three, near death, did not confess; they only said, "This was the High Temple's divine spirit teaching your servant to speak these words.

sentences.zh: 」主獄者乃以三人相為主使讞上。

translations.literal: " The chief interrogators thereupon submitted a verdict report that the three had been each other's masterminds.
translations.idiomatic: " The chief interrogators thereupon submitted a verdict report that the three had been each other's masterminds.

sentences.zh: 詔皆戍煙瘴，時來得橫州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all exiled to malarial regions; Shilai was assigned Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered all exiled to malarial regions; Wu Shilai was assigned Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，召復故官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was recalled and restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longqing he was recalled and restored to his former office.

sentences.zh: 進工科給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Supervising Secretary in the Bureau of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supervising Secretary in the Bureau of Works.

sentences.zh: 條上治河事宜，又薦譚綸、俞大猷、戚繼光宜用之薊鎮，專練邊兵，省諸鎮征調。

translations.literal: He itemized and submitted river-control matters; he also recommended Tan Lun, Yu Dayou, and Qi Jiguang to be used at Jizhou garrison, devoted to drilling border troops and reducing levy drafts from the various garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: He itemized and submitted river-control matters; he also recommended Tan Lun, Yu Dayou, and Qi Jiguang to be used at Jizhou garrison, devoted to drilling border troops and reducing levy drafts from the various garrisons.

sentences.zh: 帝皆從之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted all of it.

sentences.zh: 撫治鄖陽。

translations.literal: He was assigned to govern and pacify Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to govern and pacify Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 僉都御史劉秉仁被劾且調用，時來言秉仁薦太監李芳，無大臣節，秉仁遂坐罷。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Bingren was impeached and about to be transferred; Shilai said Bingren had recommended eunuch Li Fang and lacked the integrity of a grand minister; Bingren was thereupon dismissed on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Bingren was impeached and about to be transferred; Wu Shilai said Liu Bingren had recommended eunuch Li Fang and lacked the integrity of a grand minister; Liu Bingren was thereupon dismissed on that account.

sentences.zh: 帝免喪既久，臨朝未嘗發言，時來上保泰九劄，報聞。

translations.literal: The emperor had been out of mourning for a long time yet had never spoken at court; Shilai submitted nine memorials on preserving stability; acknowledgment was returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had been out of mourning for a long time yet had never spoken at court; Wu Shilai submitted nine memorials on preserving stability; acknowledgment was returned.

sentences.zh: 尋擢順天府丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Magistrate of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Vice Magistrate of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年，拜南京右僉都御史提督操江。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longqing he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing, directing river patrol forces at Caojiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Longqing he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing, directing river patrol forces at Caojiang.

sentences.zh: 移巡撫廣東。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Guangdong as grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to govern Guangdong as grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 將行，薦所屬有司至五十九人。

translations.literal: Before departing, he recommended subordinate officials—up to fifty-nine persons.
translations.idiomatic: Before departing, he recommended subordinate officials—up to fifty-nine persons.

sentences.zh: 給事中光懋等劾其濫舉。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Guang Mao and others impeached him for indiscriminate recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Guang Mao and others impeached him for indiscriminate recommendation.

sentences.zh: 會高拱掌吏部，雅不喜時來，貶雲南副使。

translations.literal: As it happened Gao Gong was in charge of the Ministry of Personnel and had never liked Shilai; he was demoted to Vice Commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: As it happened Gao Gong was in charge of the Ministry of Personnel and had never liked Wu Shilai; Wu Shilai was demoted to Vice Commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 復為拱門生給事中韓楫所劾，落職閑住。

translations.literal: He was again impeached by Supervising Secretary Han Ji, Gao Gong's disciple, and was stripped of office to live in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He was again impeached by Supervising Secretary Han Ji, Gao Gong's disciple, and was stripped of office to live in retirement.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十二年，始起湖廣副使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Wanli he was at last raised to Vice Commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Wanli he was at last raised to Vice Commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 俄擢左通政，歷吏部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Left Administration Commissioner and successively served as Left Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Left Administration Commissioner and successively served as Left Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十五年拜左都御史。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 誠意伯劉世延怙惡，數抗朝令，時來劾之，下所司訊治。

translations.literal: Sincerity Earl Liu Shiyan relied on his wickedness and repeatedly resisted court orders; Shilai impeached him, and he was sent to the responsible office for interrogation and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Sincerity Earl Liu Shiyan relied on his wickedness and repeatedly resisted court orders; Wu Shilai impeached him, and Liu Shiyan was sent to the responsible office for interrogation and punishment.

sentences.zh: 時來初以直竄，聲振朝端。

translations.literal: Shilai at first rose to fame through upright denunciation that brought exile, and his reputation shook the court.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shilai at first rose to fame through upright denunciation that brought exile, and his reputation shook the court.

sentences.zh: 再遭折挫，沈淪十余年。

translations.literal: Again he suffered setbacks and sank into obscurity for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He suffered further reversals and languished in obscurity for more than a decade.

sentences.zh: 晚節不能自堅，委蛇執政間。

translations.literal: In his later years he could not hold firm to himself and wavered among those in power.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he failed to hold his course and drifted among the men who held power.

sentences.zh: 連為饒伸、薛敷教、王麟趾、史孟麟、趙南星、王繼光所劾，時來亦連乞休歸。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly impeached by Rao Shen, Xue Fujiao, Wang Linzhi, Shi Menglin, Zhao Nanxing, and Wang Jiguang; Shilai also repeatedly asked to retire and return home.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached again and again by Rao Shen, Xue Fujiao, Wang Linzhi, Shi Menglin, Zhao Nanxing, and Wang Jiguang, and Wu Shilai too repeatedly petitioned to retire and go home.

sentences.zh: 未出都，卒。

translations.literal: Before he had left the capital, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died before he could leave the capital.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚忠恪。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Zhongke.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Zhongke, Loyal and Reverent.

sentences.zh: 尋為禮部郎中於孔兼所論，奪謚。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, through a memorial by Yu Kongjian, a bureau director in the Ministry of Rites, his posthumous title was revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yu Kongjian, a bureau director in the Ministry of Rites, memorialized against him, and his posthumous title was stripped away.

sentences.zh: 張翀，字子儀，柳州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Chong, styled Ziyi, was a native of Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong, styled Ziyi, came from Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十二年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the thirty-second year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-second year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事。

translations.literal: Appointed as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 疾嚴嵩父子亂政，抗章劾之。

translations.literal: Resenting the father and son Yan Song for corrupting governance, he submitted a defiant memorial impeaching them.
translations.idiomatic: Outraged by the father-and-son Yan Song's corruption of government, he submitted a bold memorial impeaching them.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：

translations.literal: The gist read:
translations.idiomatic: The gist of it read:

sentences.zh: 竊見大學士嵩貴則極人臣，富則甲天下。

translations.literal: I have observed that Grand Secretary Song, in rank, has reached the pinnacle of subjecthood, and in wealth surpasses all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that Grand Secretary Yan Song has risen to the highest rank a subject can hold and grown wealthier than anyone in the realm.

sentences.zh: 子為侍郎，孫為錦衣、中書，賓客滿朝班，親姻盡朱紫。

translations.literal: His son is a vice minister, his grandsons hold posts in the Embroidered Uniform Guard and as secretaries of the Grand Secretariat; his clients fill the court ranks, and his kin by marriage all wear crimson and purple.
translations.idiomatic: His son is a vice minister; his grandsons serve in the Embroidered Uniform Guard and as secretaries of the Grand Secretariat. His clients pack the court, and his relatives by marriage all wear the crimson and purple of high office.

sentences.zh: 犬馬尚知報主，乃嵩則不然。

translations.literal: Even dogs and horses know how to repay their master—yet Song is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Even dogs and horses know how to repay their master—yet Yan Song does not.

sentences.zh: 臣試以邊防、財賦、人才三大政言之。

translations.literal: Your subject will try to speak of this through the three great policies: frontier defense, fiscal revenue, and talent.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject will take up the matter under three great headings of state policy: frontier defense, fiscal revenue, and the cultivation of talent.

sentences.zh: 國家所恃為屏翰者，邊鎮也。

translations.literal: What the state relies on as its screen and shield are the frontier garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier garrisons are what the state relies on as its shield and bulwark.

sentences.zh: 自嵩輔政，文武將吏率由賄進。

translations.literal: Since Song became chief minister, civil and military officers have generally advanced through bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yan Song took power as chief minister, civil and military officers have generally won promotion through bribery.

sentences.zh: 其始不核名實，但通關節，即與除授。

translations.literal: At first he did not verify names against reality—if one merely had connections, an appointment was granted.
translations.idiomatic: At first he never checked whether a man's reputation matched his ability; if one merely had the right connections, an appointment followed.

sentences.zh: 其後不論功次，但勤問遺，即被超遷。

translations.literal: Later, merit and seniority were disregarded—if one diligently offered gifts, one was promoted ahead of others.
translations.idiomatic: Later he ignored merit and seniority altogether; if one kept the gifts flowing, he was promoted out of turn.

sentences.zh: 托名修邊建堡，覆軍者得蔭子，濫殺者得轉官。

translations.literal: Under the pretext of fortifying the frontier and building border forts, those who lost their armies obtained ennoblement for their sons, and those who killed recklessly were transferred to higher posts.
translations.idiomatic: Under the pretext of strengthening the frontier and building border forts, commanders who lost whole armies won hereditary honors for their sons, and men who killed recklessly were transferred to higher posts.

sentences.zh: 公肆詆欺，交相販鬻。

translations.literal: They openly slandered and deceived one another and traded offices back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: They openly slandered and deceived one another and traded offices among themselves.

sentences.zh: 而祖宗二百年防邊之計盡廢壞矣。

translations.literal: And the two-hundred-year frontier defense plan of our ancestors has been completely ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The two-hundred-year frontier defense plan of our ancestors has been utterly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 戶部歲發邊餉，本以贍軍。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue disburses frontier pay each year, originally to support the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the Ministry of Revenue sends out frontier pay, funds meant to sustain the troops.

sentences.zh: 自嵩輔政，朝出度支之門，暮入奸臣之府。

translations.literal: Since Song became chief minister, it goes out the gate of the revenue office in the morning and by evening enters the traitor's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yan Song took power, that money leaves the revenue office in the morning and by evening has entered the traitor's mansion.

sentences.zh: 輸邊者四，饋嵩者六。

translations.literal: Four parts go to the frontier, six parts are presented to Song.
translations.idiomatic: Four parts reach the frontier; six parts are lavished on Yan Song.

sentences.zh: 臣每過長安街，見嵩門下無非邊鎮使人。

translations.literal: Whenever your subject passes Chang'an Street, he sees nothing but envoys from frontier garrisons at Song's gate.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I pass Chang'an Street, I see nothing at Yan Song's gate but envoys from the frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 未見其父，先饋其子。

translations.literal: Before seeing the father, they first present gifts to the son.
translations.idiomatic: Before they have even seen the father, they already present gifts to the son.

sentences.zh: 未見其子，先饋家人。

translations.literal: Before seeing the son, they first present gifts to his household retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Before they have even seen the son, they already present gifts to his household retainers.

sentences.zh: 家人嚴年富已逾數十萬，嵩家可知。

translations.literal: The household retainer Yan Nian's wealth already exceeds several hundred thousand—Song's household fortune may readily be inferred.
translations.idiomatic: The household retainer Yan Nian alone is already worth more than several hundred thousand; Yan Song's household fortune needs no guessing.

sentences.zh: 私藏充溢，半屬軍儲；

translations.literal: Private hoards overflow, half of them drawn from military stores;
translations.idiomatic: Private hoards overflow with wealth, half of it drawn from military stores;

sentences.zh: 邊卒凍餒，不保朝夕。

translations.literal: Frontier soldiers freeze and starve, not assured of even a day's survival.
translations.idiomatic: while frontier soldiers freeze and starve, unsure whether they will live to see the next day.

sentences.zh: 而祖宗二百年豢養之軍盡耗弱矣。

translations.literal: And the army our ancestors nourished for two hundred years has been utterly weakened.
translations.idiomatic: The army our ancestors nourished for two hundred years has been utterly drained of strength.

sentences.zh: 邊防既隳。
