translations.literal: Frontier defense is already ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier defense is already in ruins.

sentences.zh: 邊儲既虛，使人才足供陛下用，猶不足憂也。

translations.literal: Frontier stores are already depleted; if talent were sufficient to serve Your Majesty's needs, there would still be no cause for alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier stores are already empty; if talent were still abundant enough to serve Your Majesty, there would be less cause for alarm.

sentences.zh: 自嵩輔政，藐蔑名器，私營囊橐。

translations.literal: Since Song became chief minister, he has scorned honored appointments and privately filled his purse.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yan Song took power, he has treated honored offices with contempt and privately stuffed his purse.

sentences.zh: 世蕃以狙獪資，倚父虎狼之勢，招權罔利，獸攫烏鈔。

translations.literal: Shifan, with his cunning and treachery, relies on his father's tiger-and-wolf power to grasp authority and pursue illicit profit, like a beast seizing and a bird scooping up wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan, cunning and treacherous by nature, relies on his father's tiger-and-wolf power to grasp authority and pursue illicit profit, snatching wealth like a beast and a bird of prey.

sentences.zh: 無恥之徒，絡繹奔走，靡然成風，有如狂易。

translations.literal: Shameless men rush back and forth in endless streams, and it has become the prevailing custom, like a frenzy of madness.
translations.idiomatic: Shameless men rush to and fro in an unending stream until the practice has become the prevailing custom, like a collective madness.

sentences.zh: 而祖宗二百年培養之人才盡敗壞矣。

translations.literal: And the talent our ancestors cultivated for two hundred years has been utterly ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The talent our ancestors cultivated for two hundred years has been utterly ruined.

sentences.zh: 夫嵩險足以傾人，詐足以惑世，辨足以亂政，才足以濟奸。

translations.literal: Song's viciousness is enough to overturn men, his deceit enough to bewilder the world, his eloquence enough to disorder governance, and his talent enough to assist villainy.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song's viciousness is enough to overturn men, his deceit enough to bewilder the world, his eloquence enough to disorder government, and his talent enough to serve villainy.

sentences.zh: 附己者加諸膝，異己者墜之淵。

translations.literal: Those who attached themselves to him he placed on his knee; those who differed from him he cast into the abyss.
translations.idiomatic: Those who attached themselves to him he drew up onto his knee; those who opposed him he cast into the abyss.

sentences.zh: 箝天下口使不敢言，而其惡日以恣。

translations.literal: He clamped shut the mouths of all under Heaven so none dared speak, and his wickedness grew daily more unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: He clamped shut the mouths of the realm so that none dared speak, and his wickedness grew more unrestrained by the day.

sentences.zh: 此忠義之士，所以搤腕憤激，懷深長之憂者也。

translations.literal: This is why loyal and righteous men clench their fists in rage, stirred to fury, and harbor deep and lingering grief.
translations.idiomatic: This is why loyal and righteous men clench their fists in fury and carry a deep, lingering grief in their hearts.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠賜斥譴，以快眾憤，則緣邊將士不戰而氣自倍，百司庶府不令而政自新。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty would truly bestow dismissal and rebuke to satisfy public outrage, then frontier troops would double in spirit without fighting, and the hundred offices and various departments would renew their governance without being commanded.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would truly dismiss and rebuke him to satisfy public outrage, frontier troops would double in spirit without fighting, and the hundred offices and departments would renew their governance without being commanded.

sentences.zh: 書奏，逮下詔獄拷訊，謫戍都勻。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, he was arrested and sent to the imperial prison for interrogation under torture, then banished to serve as garrison troops at Duyun.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Zhang Chong was arrested and sent to the imperial prison for interrogation under torture, then banished to military service at Duyun.

sentences.zh: 穆宗嗣位，召為吏部主事，再遷大理少卿。

translations.literal: When Muzong succeeded to the throne, he was recalled as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, then promoted again to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong succeeded to the throne, Zhang Chong was recalled as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel and then promoted again to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年春，以右僉都御史巡撫南、贛。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Longqing, he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and sent to govern Nan and Gan as grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Longqing he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and sent to govern Nan and Gan as grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 所部萬羊山跨湖廣、福建、廣東境，故盜藪，四方商民種藍其間。

translations.literal: Within his jurisdiction Mount Wanyang straddles the borders of Huguang, Fujian, and Guangdong—a former bandit lair where merchants from all quarters cultivated indigo there.
translations.idiomatic: Within his jurisdiction Mount Wanyang straddles the borders of Huguang, Fujian, and Guangdong. It had long been a bandit haunt, and merchants from all quarters cultivated indigo there.

sentences.zh: 至是，盜出劫，翀遣守備董龍剿之。

translations.literal: At this time bandits came out to plunder; Chong dispatched the garrison commander Dong Long to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: At this point bandits came out to plunder, and Zhang Chong dispatched the garrison commander Dong Long to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 龍聲言搜山，諸藍戶大恐。

translations.literal: Long proclaimed he would search the mountains, and the indigo cultivators were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Long announced that he would search the mountains, and the indigo cultivators were terrified.

sentences.zh: 盜因煽之，嘯聚千余人。

translations.literal: The bandits took advantage to incite them, and they rallied more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits incited them, and more than a thousand men rallied with a war cry.

sentences.zh: 兵部令二鎮撫臣協議撫剿之宜，久乃定。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War ordered the two regional commanders to consult on whether pacification or suppression was appropriate; only after a long time was a plan settled.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War ordered the two regional commanders to consult on whether to pacify or suppress the uprising, and only after a long delay was a plan settled.

sentences.zh: 南雄劇盜黃朝祖流劫諸縣，轉掠湖廣，勢甚熾。

translations.literal: The vicious bandit Huang Chaozu of Nanxiong raided and plundered through various counties, then turned to loot Huguang; his power grew very fierce.
translations.idiomatic: The vicious bandit Huang Chaozu of Nanxiong raided county after county, then turned to plunder Huguang, and his power grew very fierce.

sentences.zh: 翀討擒之。

translations.literal: Chong pursued and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong pursued him and captured him.

sentences.zh: 移撫湖廣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Huguang as grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to govern Huguang as grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 召拜大理卿，進兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, then promoted to Right Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, then promoted to Right Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 以侍養歸。

translations.literal: He returned home to care for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，起故官，督漕運。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli he was recalled to his former office and put in charge of grain transport on the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wanli reign he was recalled to his former office and put in charge of grain transport on the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 召為刑部右侍郎，不拜，連章乞休。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Right Vice Minister of Justice but declined the appointment and repeatedly submitted memorials asking to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Right Vice Minister of Justice but declined the appointment and repeatedly submitted memorials asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，贈兵部尚書，謚忠簡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of War with the posthumous title Zhongjian.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of War and given the posthumous title Zhongjian, Loyal and Unadorned.

sentences.zh: 董傳策，字原漢，松江華亭人。

translations.literal: Dong Chuance, styled Yuanhan, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chuance, styled Yuanhan, came from Huating in Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十九年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the twenty-ninth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twenty-ninth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 除刑部主事。

translations.literal: Appointed as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 三十七年抗疏劾大學士嚴嵩，略言：

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he submitted a defiant memorial impeaching Grand Secretary Yan Song; the gist read:
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he submitted a bold memorial impeaching Grand Secretary Yan Song. The gist read:

sentences.zh: 嵩諗惡誤國，陛下豈不洞燭其奸？

translations.literal: Song's persistent wickedness has harmed the state—does Your Majesty not see through his treachery clearly?
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song's persistent wickedness has harmed the state—does Your Majesty not see through his treachery with perfect clarity?

sentences.zh: 特以輔政故，尚為優容，令自省改。

translations.literal: Only because he assists in governance has he still been treated with forbearance, that he might examine himself and reform.
translations.idiomatic: Only because he assists in governance has he still been treated with forbearance, in the hope that he would examine himself and reform.

sentences.zh: 而嵩恬不知戒，負恩愈深。

translations.literal: Yet Song remains heedless of warning and has grown ever deeper in betrayal of grace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yan Song remains heedless of warning and has grown ever deeper in his betrayal of imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 居位一日，天下受一日之害。

translations.literal: For each day he holds office, the realm suffers a day's harm.
translations.idiomatic: For each day he holds office, the realm suffers a day's harm.

sentences.zh: 臣竊痛之。

translations.literal: Your subject is privately grieved by this.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject is deeply grieved by this.

sentences.zh: 夫邊疆督撫將帥欲得士卒死力，必資財用。

translations.literal: For frontier grand coordinators, governors, and generals to obtain their soldiers' utmost effort, they must have funds at their disposal.
translations.idiomatic: For frontier grand coordinators, governors, and generals to win their soldiers' utmost effort, they must have funds at their disposal.

sentences.zh: 今諸邊軍餉歲費百萬，強半賂嵩。

translations.literal: Today frontier military pay costs a million taels each year, and more than half is used to bribe Song.
translations.idiomatic: Today frontier military pay costs a million taels each year, and more than half of it is used to bribe Yan Song.

sentences.zh: 遂令軍士饑疲，寇賊深入。

translations.literal: Thus soldiers grow hungry and exhausted, and bandits and invaders push deep into the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The result is that soldiers grow hungry and exhausted while bandits and invaders push deep into the realm.

sentences.zh: 此其壞邊防之罪一也。

translations.literal: This is the first of his crimes in ruining frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first of his crimes in ruining frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 吏、兵二部持選簿就嵩填註。

translations.literal: The two ministries of Personnel and War bring the selection registers to Song for him to fill in appointments.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministries of Personnel and War bring the selection registers to Yan Song for him to fill in appointments.

sentences.zh: 文選郎萬寀、職方郎方祥甘聽指使，不異卒隸。

translations.literal: The Bureau Director Wan Cai of the Civil Appointments section and the Bureau Director Fang Xiang of the Military Appointments section willingly obey his orders, no different from soldier-servants.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Cai, bureau director of the Civil Appointments section, and Fang Xiang, bureau director of the Military Appointments section, willingly obey his orders like common soldier-servants.

sentences.zh: 都門諺語至以「文武管家」目之。

translations.literal: A proverb in the capital even calls them "the civil and military house stewards."
translations.idiomatic: A proverb in the capital even calls them "the civil and military house stewards."

sentences.zh: 此其鬻官爵之罪二也。

translations.literal: This is the second of his crimes in selling offices and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second of his crimes in selling offices and ranks.

sentences.zh: 侍郎劉伯躍以采木行部，擅斂民財及郡縣贓罪，輦輸嵩家，前後不絕。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Liu Boyue, while traveling his jurisdiction collecting timber, extorted the people's wealth and diverted county and prefectural illicit gains, conveying them to Song's household without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Liu Boyue, while touring his jurisdiction to collect timber, extorted the people's wealth and diverted county and prefectural illicit gains, sending them in an unbroken stream to Yan Song's household.

sentences.zh: 其他有司破冒攘敚，入獻於嵩者更不可數計。

translations.literal: Other officials who violated regulations and seized by force what they presented to Song are more than can be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Other officials who broke regulations and seized wealth by force to present to Yan Song are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 嵩家私藏，富於公帑。

translations.literal: Song's private hoards are richer than the state treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song's private hoards are richer than the state treasury.

sentences.zh: 此其蠹國用之罪三也。

translations.literal: This is the third of his crimes in draining the state's resources.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third of his crimes in draining the state's resources.

sentences.zh: 趙文華以罪放逐，嵩沒其囊橐巨萬，而令人護送南還。

translations.literal: Zhao Wenhua was banished for his crimes; Song confiscated his baggage worth tens of thousands, then had men escort him south to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenhua was banished for his crimes; Yan Song confiscated his baggage worth tens of thousands, then had men escort him south to return home.

sentences.zh: 恐喝州縣，私役民夫，致道路驛騷，公私煩費。

translations.literal: They intimidated and threatened prefectures and counties, privately impressed corvée laborers, causing turmoil along the roads and courier routes and burdensome expense to both public and private interests.
translations.idiomatic: They intimidated prefectures and counties, privately impressed corvée laborers, and caused turmoil along the roads and courier routes at great public and private expense.

sentences.zh: 此其黨罪人之罪四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth of his crimes in protecting a convicted criminal.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth of his crimes in protecting a convicted criminal.

sentences.zh: 天下藩臬諸司，歲時問遺，動以千計，勢不得不掊克小民。

translations.literal: Officials throughout the realm—provincial governors, surveillance commissioners, and all other departments—send seasonal gifts in the thousands; they cannot but squeeze and despoil the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial governors, surveillance commissioners, and officials throughout the realm send seasonal gifts by the thousands; they cannot but squeeze and despoil the common people.

sentences.zh: 民財日殫，嵩貲日積。

translations.literal: The people's wealth is daily exhausted, while Song's fortune daily accumulates.
translations.idiomatic: The people's wealth is daily exhausted while Yan Song's fortune daily accumulates.

sentences.zh: 於是水陸舟車載還其鄉，月無虛日。

translations.literal: Consequently, by river, land, cart, and boat, wealth was transported back to his native district—there was not a single month without it.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth was therefore transported back to his native district by river, road, cart, and boat—not a month passed without it.

sentences.zh: 所至要索供億，勢如虎狼。

translations.literal: Wherever they passed they demanded supplies and provisioning, with the ferocity of tigers and wolves.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever they passed they demanded supplies and provisioning with the ferocity of tigers and wolves.

sentences.zh: 此其騷驛傳之罪五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth of his crimes in harassing the courier system.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth of his crimes in harassing the courier system.

sentences.zh: 嵩久握重權，灸手而熱。

translations.literal: Song has long held heavy power—too hot to touch.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song has long held heavy power—too hot to touch.

sentences.zh: 幹進無恥之徒，附亶逐穢，麕集其門。

translations.literal: Shameless men seeking advancement attached themselves to his filth and crowded his gate like a herd.
translations.idiomatic: Shameless men seeking advancement clung to his filth and crowded his gate like a herd.

sentences.zh: 致士風日偷，官箴日喪。

translations.literal: It caused the spirit of the scholar-official class to daily decay and official integrity to daily perish.
translations.idiomatic: It caused the spirit of the scholar-official class to decay by the day and official integrity to perish by the day.

sentences.zh: 此其壞人才之罪六也。

translations.literal: This is the sixth of his crimes in ruining talent.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sixth of his crimes in ruining talent.

sentences.zh: 嵩以蔽欺行其專權，生死予奪惟意所為。

translations.literal: Song exercises his monopoly on power through concealment and deception; life and death, granting and seizing—all are as he wills.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song exercises his monopoly on power through concealment and deception; life and death, granting and seizing—all are as he wills.

sentences.zh: 而世蕃又以無賴之子，竊威助惡。

translations.literal: Shifan, moreover, as a worthless son, usurped his father's authority to abet evil.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan, moreover, as a worthless son, usurped his father's authority to abet evil.

sentences.zh: 父子肆兇，中外飲憤。

translations.literal: Father and son ran rampant in wickedness, and within and outside the court all swallowed their rage.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son ran rampant in wickedness, and within and outside the court all swallowed their rage in silence.

sentences.zh: 有臣如此，非國法可容。

translations.literal: To have ministers such as these is not what state law can tolerate.
translations.idiomatic: To have ministers such as these is not what state law can tolerate.

sentences.zh: 臣待罪刑曹，宜詰奸慝。

translations.literal: Your subject holds office in the Ministry of Justice under a charge of guilt and ought to interrogate treacherous villains.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject holds office in the Ministry of Justice and ought to interrogate treacherous villains.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠不惜嚴氏以謝天下，則臣亦何惜一死以謝權奸！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty would truly not spare the Yan clan to answer to the realm, then what would your subject spare in giving his life to answer to the power-hoarding villain!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would truly not spare the Yan clan to answer to the realm, then what would your subject spare in giving his life to answer to this power-hoarding villain!

sentences.zh: 疏入，下詔獄。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, he was sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Dong Chuance was sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 謫戍南寧。

translations.literal: Relegated to garrison duty at Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: He was relegated to garrison duty at Nanning.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，召復故官。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, he was summoned and restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, Dong Chuance was summoned back and restored to his former office.

sentences.zh: 歷郎中。

translations.literal: He served through the rank of director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the rank of director.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年累遷南京大理卿，進工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Longqing, through repeated promotions he reached Chief Judge of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review and was advanced to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Longqing reign, through successive promotions he became Chief Judge of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review and was then promoted to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 萬歷元年就改禮部。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wanli he was immediately transferred to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Wanli reign he was immediately transferred to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 言官劾傳策受人賄，免歸。

translations.literal: Censorial officials impeached Chuance for accepting bribes; he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials impeached Dong Chuance for accepting bribes, and he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 繩下過急，竟為家奴所害。

translations.literal: In binding his household he was too severe, and in the end he was killed by a domestic slave.
translations.idiomatic: In disciplining his household he was excessively harsh, and in the end he was killed by a domestic slave.

sentences.zh: 鄒應龍，字雲卿，長安人。

translations.literal: Zou Yinglong, styled Yunqing, was a native of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Yinglong, styled Yunqing, came from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十五年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the thirty-fifth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-fifth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授行人，擢御史。

translations.literal: Appointed as a courier official, he was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a courier official and soon promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩擅政久，廷臣攻之者輒得禍，相戒莫敢言。

translations.literal: Yan Song had monopolized power for a long time; court officials who attacked him invariably met disaster, and people warned one another, none daring to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song had monopolized power for a long time; court officials who attacked him invariably met with disaster, and people warned one another until none dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 而應龍知帝眷已潛移，其子世蕃益貪縱，可攻而去也，乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: But Yinglong knew the emperor's favor had quietly shifted; Song's son Shifan had grown ever more greedy and unrestrained—he could be attacked and removed—and so he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: But Zou Yinglong perceived that the emperor's favor had quietly shifted; Yan Song's son Yan Shifan had grown ever more greedy and unrestrained, and could now be attacked and removed. He therefore submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 工部侍郎嚴世蕃憑藉父權，專利無厭。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Works Yan Shifan relies on his father's power and seeks profit without satiety.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Works Yan Shifan relies on his father's power and seeks profit without limit.

sentences.zh: 私擅爵賞，廣致賂遺。

translations.literal: He privately usurps conferrals of titles and rewards and widely solicits bribes and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He privately usurps conferrals of titles and rewards and widely solicits bribes and gifts.

sentences.zh: 使選法敗壞，市道公行。

translations.literal: He causes the standards of selection to rot, and the marketplace of favor to operate openly.
translations.idiomatic: He has corrupted the standards of official selection until the marketplace of favor operates openly.

sentences.zh: 群小競趨，要價轉鉅。

translations.literal: Petty men race to flock to him, and the price demanded grows ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men race to flock to him, and the prices demanded grow ever larger.

sentences.zh: 刑部主事項治元以萬三千金轉吏部，舉人潘鴻業以二千二百金得知州。

translations.literal: A principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice, Xiang Zhiyuan, transferred to the Ministry of Personnel for thirteen thousand gold; the provincial graduate Pan Hongye paid two thousand two hundred gold to obtain a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Zhiyuan, a principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice, bought transfer to the Ministry of Personnel for thirteen thousand taels; the provincial graduate Pan Hongye paid two thousand two hundred taels to obtain a prefectural post.

sentences.zh: 夫司屬郡吏賂以千萬，則大而公卿方嶽，又安知紀極？

translations.literal: If subordinate officials of a department can be bribed for thousands and tens of thousands, then how can one know the limit for great ministers, dukes, and governors?
translations.idiomatic: If subordinate officials can be bought for thousands upon thousands of taels, who can say where the limits lie for grand ministers, dukes, and provincial governors?

sentences.zh: 平時交通贓賄，為之居間者不下百十余人，而其子錦衣嚴鵠、中書嚴鴻、家人嚴年、幕客中書羅龍文為甚。

translations.literal: In ordinary times those who traffic in filthy bribes and serve as go-betweens for him number no fewer than a hundred or more; among them his son the brocade-clad guard Yan Hu, Secretariat drafter Yan Hong, household retainer Yan Nian, and secretarial adviser Luo Longwen are especially so.
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary times those who traffic in illicit bribes and serve as go-betweens for him number well over a hundred; among them his son the brocade-clad guard Yan Hu, Secretariat drafter Yan Hong, household retainer Yan Nian, and secretarial adviser Luo Longwen are the worst offenders.

sentences.zh: 年尤桀黠，士大夫無恥者至呼為鶴山先生。

translations.literal: Nian was especially cunning and vicious; shameless scholar-officials even addressed him as Master Heshan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Nian was especially cunning and vicious; shameless scholar-officials even addressed him as Master Heshan.

sentences.zh: 遇嵩生日，年輒獻萬金為壽。

translations.literal: Whenever Song's birthday came, Nian would present ten thousand gold as birthday tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yan Song's birthday came, Yan Nian would present ten thousand taels as birthday tribute.

sentences.zh: 臧獲富侈若是，主人當何如？

translations.literal: If bond servants are rich and extravagant to such a degree, what must their master be like?
translations.idiomatic: If bond servants are rich and extravagant to such a degree, what must their master be like?

sentences.zh: 嵩父子故籍袁州，乃廣置良田美宅於南京、揚州，無慮數十所，以豪仆嚴冬主之。

translations.literal: The Song father and son were originally registered in Yuanzhou, yet they widely established fine fields and splendid dwellings in Nanjing and Yangzhou—no fewer than several tens of estates—entrusted to their overbearing servant Yan Dong.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Yan Song father and son were originally registered in Yuanzhou, they established fine fields and splendid dwellings across Nanjing and Yangzhou—several dozen estates in all—entrusted to their overbearing servant Yan Dong.

sentences.zh: 抑勒侵奪，民怨入骨。

translations.literal: Through extortion and seizure, popular resentment penetrated to the bone.
translations.idiomatic: Through extortion and seizure, popular resentment ran bone-deep.

sentences.zh: 外地牟利若是，鄉里又何如？

translations.literal: If profit is sought abroad to such a degree, what must things be like in their home district?
translations.idiomatic: If they profit abroad to such a degree, what must things be like in their home district?

sentences.zh: 尤可異者，世蕃喪母，陛下以嵩年高，特留侍養，令鵠扶櫬南還。

translations.literal: What is especially strange is that when Shifan was in mourning for his mother, Your Majesty, because Song was advanced in years, specially allowed him to remain behind and serve in nurturing, ordering Hu to escort the bier south to return home.
translations.idiomatic: What is especially strange is that when Yan Shifan was in mourning for his mother, Your Majesty, because Yan Song was advanced in years, specially allowed him to remain at court to care for his father, ordering Yan Hu to escort the bier south to their native place.

sentences.zh: 世蕃乃聚狎客，擁艷姬，恒舞酣歌，人紀滅絕。

translations.literal: Shifan instead gathered frivolous guests, surrounded himself with beautiful women, and constantly danced and sang in drunken revelry—human norms were extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shifan instead gathered frivolous guests, surrounded himself with beautiful women, and constantly danced and sang in drunken revelry, extinguishing every human norm.

sentences.zh: 至鵠之無知，則以祖母喪為奇貨。

translations.literal: As for Hu's want of understanding, he treated his grandmother's mourning as a rare commodity.
translations.idiomatic: As for Yan Hu's want of understanding, he treated his grandmother's funeral as a rare opportunity for profit.

sentences.zh: 所至驛騷，要索百故。

translations.literal: Wherever he went, he stirred up the relay stations and made demands under countless pretexts.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went he stirred up the relay stations and made demands under countless pretexts.

sentences.zh: 諸司承奉，郡邑為空。

translations.literal: All offices rushed to serve him, and prefectures and counties were drained empty.
translations.idiomatic: Every office rushed to serve him, and prefectures and counties were drained empty.

sentences.zh: 今天下水旱頻仍，南北多警。

translations.literal: Today floods and droughts recur frequently, and alarms are many north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Today floods and droughts recur frequently, and alarms multiply north and south.

sentences.zh: 而世蕃父子方日事掊克，內外百司莫不竭民脂膏，塞彼溪壑。

translations.literal: Yet the Shifan father and son are just then daily engaged in squeezing and exaction; within and without, all the hundred offices exhaust the fat and cream of the people to fill those ravines and gullies.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Yan Shifan father and son are daily engaged in squeezing and exaction; within and without, all offices exhaust the people's substance to fill their bottomless gullets.

sentences.zh: 民安得不貧？

translations.literal: How can the people not grow poor?
translations.idiomatic: How can the people not grow poor?

sentences.zh: 國安得不病？

translations.literal: How can the state not sicken?
translations.idiomatic: How can the state not sicken?

sentences.zh: 天人災變安得不叠至也？

translations.literal: How can catastrophes and portents between Heaven and humanity not arrive one upon another?
translations.idiomatic: How can catastrophes and portents between Heaven and humanity not arrive one upon another?

sentences.zh: 臣請斬世蕃首懸之於市，以為人臣兇橫不忠之戒。

translations.literal: Your subject requests that Shifan's head be cut off and hung in the marketplace as a warning to ministers who are violent, overbearing, and disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject requests that Yan Shifan's head be cut off and hung in the marketplace as a warning to ministers who are violent, overbearing, and disloyal.

sentences.zh: 茍臣一言失實，甘伏顯戮。

translations.literal: If a single word of your subject's proves false, he willingly submits to public execution.
translations.idiomatic: If a single word of this proves false, your subject willingly submits to public execution.

sentences.zh: 嵩溺愛惡子，召賂市權，亦宜亟放歸田，用清政本。

translations.literal: Song dotes on his wicked son and summons bribes to trade for power; he too ought quickly to be released to retire to his fields, so as to cleanse the foundations of government.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song dotes on his wicked son and invites bribes to trade for power; he too ought quickly to be dismissed to retire to his fields, so as to cleanse the foundations of government.

sentences.zh: 帝頗知世蕃居喪淫縱，心惡之。

translations.literal: The emperor was rather aware that Shifan in mourning was lustful and unrestrained, and he felt disgust in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was already aware that Yan Shifan had been lustful and unrestrained during mourning, and he felt revulsion toward him.

sentences.zh: 會方士藍道行以扶乩得幸，帝密問輔臣賢否。

translations.literal: It happened that the Taoist adept Lan Daoxing gained favor through planchette divination, and the emperor secretly asked whether the chief minister was worthy.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the Taoist adept Lan Daoxing gained favor through planchette divination, and the emperor secretly asked whether the chief minister was worthy.

sentences.zh: 道行詐為乩語，具言嵩父子弄權狀，帝由是疏嵩而任徐階。

translations.literal: Daoxing feigned a planchette utterance and fully set forth how the Song father and son manipulated power; the emperor thereby grew distant from Song and entrusted Xu Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Daoxing feigned a planchette utterance and fully described how the Yan Song father and son manipulated power; the emperor thereby grew distant from Yan Song and entrusted Xu Jie.

sentences.zh: 及應龍奏入，遂勒嵩致仕，下世蕃等詔獄，擢應龍通政司參議。

translations.literal: When Yinglong's memorial arrived, the emperor then compelled Song to retire, sent Shifan and the rest to the prison by imperial order, and promoted Yinglong to Secretariat Reception vice director.
translations.idiomatic: When Zou Yinglong's memorial arrived, the emperor compelled Yan Song to retire, sent Yan Shifan and his associates to the imperial prison, and promoted Zou Yinglong to vice director of the Secretariat Reception Office.

sentences.zh: 然帝雖罷嵩，念其贊修玄功，意忽忽不樂，手劄諭階：「嵩已退，其子已伏辜，敢再言者，當並應龍斬之。

translations.literal: Yet although the emperor had dismissed Song, he recalled his assistance in cultivating esoteric merit, and his mood was restless and discontent; by personal note he instructed Jie: "Song has already retired, and his son has already paid the penalty; whoever dares speak further shall together with Yinglong be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Yet although the emperor had dismissed Yan Song, he recalled his assistance in cultivating esoteric merit, and his mood was restless and discontent. In a personal note he instructed Xu Jie: "Yan Song has already retired, and his son has already paid the penalty; whoever dares speak further shall together with Zou Yinglong be executed."

sentences.zh: 」應龍深自危，不敢履任，賴階調護始視事。

translations.literal: Yinglong felt deeply imperiled himself, dared not assume office, and only with Jie's protection and guidance began to perform his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Yinglong felt deeply imperiled himself and dared not assume office; only with Xu Jie's protection and guidance did he begin to perform his duties.

sentences.zh: 御史張槚巡鹽河東，不知帝指，上疏言：「陛下已顯擢應龍，而王宗茂、趙錦輩首發大奸未召，是曲突者不賞也。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Chong, inspecting the salt administration in Hedong, did not know the emperor's intent and submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty has already clearly promoted Yinglong, yet Wang Zongmao, Zhao Jin, and others who first exposed the great villain have not been summoned; this is not rewarding the man who curved the chimney."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Chong, inspecting the salt administration in Hedong, did not know the emperor's intent and submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty has already clearly promoted Zou Yinglong, yet Wang Zongmao, Zhao Jin, and others who first exposed the great villain have not been summoned—this is the case of not rewarding the man who curved the chimney."

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒，立逮至，杖六十，斥為民。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged, immediately had him seized and brought, beat him sixty blows, and expelled him as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly enraged, immediately had Zhang Chong seized and brought, beat him sixty blows, and expelled him as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 久之，世蕃誅，應龍乃自安。

translations.literal: After a long while, Shifan was executed, and only then did Yinglong feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while Yan Shifan was executed, and only then did Zou Yinglong feel secure.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，以副都御史總理江西、江南鹽屯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, as vice censor-in-chief he took general charge of salt garrisons in Jiangxi and Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign, as vice censor-in-chief he took general charge of salt garrisons in Jiangxi and Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 遷工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 鎮守雲南黔國公沐朝弼驕恣，廷議遣大臣有威望者鎮之，乃改應龍兵部侍郎兼右僉都御史巡撫雲南。

translations.literal: The Qian Principality Duke Mu Chaobi, charged with guarding Yunnan, was arrogant and willful; court deliberation decided to send a great minister of established prestige to keep him in check, and so Yinglong was changed to Vice Minister of War concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right and grand coordinator of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: The Qian Principality Duke Mu Chaobi, charged with guarding Yunnan, was arrogant and willful; court deliberation decided to send a great minister of established prestige to keep him in check, and so Zou Yinglong was appointed Vice Minister of War concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right and grand coordinator of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 至則發朝弼罪，朝弼竟被逮。

translations.literal: Upon arrival he exposed Chaobi's crimes, and Chaobi was ultimately arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Upon arrival he exposed Mu Chaobi's crimes, and Mu Chaobi was ultimately arrested.

sentences.zh: 萬歷改元，鐵索箐賊作亂，討平之。

translations.literal: When the reign title changed to Wanli, bandits at Tiesuoqing rebelled, and he suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When the reign title changed to Wanli, bandits at Tiesuoqing rebelled, and he suppressed and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 已，番人栂犭發反，合土漢兵進討，斬獲各千余人。

translations.literal: Thereafter the tribesman Mu Bo rebelled; combining tribal and Han troops he advanced to attack, beheading and capturing more than a thousand on each count.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the tribal chieftain Mu Bo rebelled; Zou Yinglong combined tribal and Han troops in an advance against him, killing and capturing more than a thousand on each count.

sentences.zh: 應龍有才氣，初以劾嚴嵩得名，驟致通顯。

translations.literal: Yinglong had talent and spirit; at first he gained fame for impeaching Yan Song and suddenly rose to high visibility.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Yinglong had talent and spirit; at first he gained fame for impeaching Yan Song and suddenly rose to high prominence.

sentences.zh: 及為太常，省牲北郊，東廠太監馮保傳呼至，導者引入，正面爇香，儼若天子。

translations.literal: When he served as Grand Master of Ceremonies, inspecting the sacrificial victims at the northern suburban altar, the Eastern Depot eunuch Feng Bao had his name called out and announced; the guide led him in, and facing forward he burned incense, just as if he were the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When he served as Grand Master of Ceremonies, inspecting the sacrificial victims at the northern suburban altar, the Eastern Depot eunuch Feng Bao had his name called out and announced; the guide led him in, and facing forward he burned incense, just as if he were the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 應龍大駭，劾保僭肆，保深銜之。

translations.literal: Yinglong was greatly alarmed and impeached Bao for presumptuous outrage; Bao deeply harbored resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Yinglong was greatly alarmed and impeached Feng Bao for presumptuous outrage; Feng Bao deeply harbored resentment against him.

sentences.zh: 至是，京察自陳，保修郤，令致仕。

translations.literal: At this point, in the metropolitan evaluation he self-reported; Bao nursed his grievance and had him ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: At this point, in the metropolitan evaluation Zou Yinglong reported on himself; Feng Bao nursed his grievance and had him ordered to retire.

sentences.zh: 臨安土官普崇明、崇新兄弟構爭。

translations.literal: The Lin'an native officials Pu Chongming and the Chongxin brothers contended in conflict.
translations.idiomatic: The Lin'an native officials Pu Chongming and Pu Chongxin, brothers, fell into conflict.

sentences.zh: 崇明引廣南儂兵為助，崇新則召交兵。

translations.literal: Chongming brought in Guangnan Nong troops as aid; Chongxin then summoned Jiao troops.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Chongming brought in Nong troops from Guangnan as allies; Pu Chongxin then summoned Annamese troops.

sentences.zh: 已，交兵退，儂兵尚留，應龍命部將楊守廉往剿。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Jiao troops withdrew, but the Nong troops remained; Yinglong ordered his subordinate general Yang Shoulian to go suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Annamese troops withdrew, but the Nong troops remained; Zou Yinglong ordered his subordinate general Yang Shoulian to go suppress them.

sentences.zh: 守廉掠村聚，殺人。

translations.literal: Shoulian plundered village settlements and killed people.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shoulian plundered village settlements and killed people.

sentences.zh: 儂賊乘之，再敗官軍，人以咎應龍。

translations.literal: The Nong bandits seized the opportunity and again defeated the government armies; people blamed Yinglong.
translations.idiomatic: The Nong bandits seized the opportunity and again defeated the government armies; people blamed Zou Yinglong.

sentences.zh: 應龍聞罷官，不俟代徑歸。

translations.literal: Yinglong heard he was dismissed from office and, without waiting for his successor, went straight home.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Yinglong heard he was dismissed from office and, without waiting for his successor, went straight home.

sentences.zh: 代者王凝欲自以為功，力排應龍。

translations.literal: His replacement Wang Ning wished to claim the credit himself and vigorously pushed aside Yinglong.
translations.idiomatic: His replacement Wang Ning wished to claim the credit himself and vigorously pushed Zou Yinglong aside.

sentences.zh: 給事中裴應章遂劾應龍僨事。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Pei Yingzhang then impeached Yinglong for ruining affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary Pei Yingzhang then impeached Zou Yinglong for bungling the campaign.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史郭廷梧雅不善應龍，勘如凝言。

translations.literal: The touring investigating censor Guo Tingwu had always disliked Yinglong; in investigation he confirmed Ning's words.
translations.idiomatic: The touring investigating censor Guo Tingwu had always disliked Zou Yinglong; in his investigation he confirmed Wang Ning's account.

sentences.zh: 應龍遂削籍，卒於家。

translations.literal: Yinglong was then struck from the rolls, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Yinglong was then struck from the rolls and died at home.

sentences.zh: 十六年，陜西巡撫王璇言應龍歿後，遺田不及數畝，遺址不過數楹，恤典未被，朝野所恨。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Shaanxi grand coordinator Wang Xuan said that after Yinglong's death the land left behind amounted to less than several mu, and the dwelling left behind to no more than several bays; posthumous honors had not been granted, and this was resented throughout court and country.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Shaanxi grand coordinator Wang Xuan reported that after Zou Yinglong's death the land he left behind amounted to less than a few mu, and his dwelling to no more than a few bays; posthumous honors had not been granted, and this was resented throughout court and country.

sentences.zh: 帝命復應龍官，予祭葬。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yinglong's office restored and granted sacrificial rites and burial honors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zou Yinglong's office restored and granted him sacrificial rites and burial honors.

sentences.zh: 張槚，江西新城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Chong, a native of Xincheng in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong came from Xincheng in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十八年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-eighth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 居臺中，敢言。

translations.literal: While serving at the censorate, he dared to speak out.
translations.idiomatic: While serving at the censorate he dared to speak out.

sentences.zh: 穆宗初，復官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Muzong, his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Muzong's reign his office was restored.

sentences.zh: 屢疏抗中官，嘗劾大學士高拱。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials resisting eunuchs and once impeached Grand Secretary Gao Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly submitted memorials resisting eunuchs and once impeached Grand Secretary Gao Gong.

sentences.zh: 拱復入閣掌吏部，槚已遷太仆少卿，坐不謹罷歸。

translations.literal: When Gong re-entered the Grand Secretariat and took charge of the Ministry of Personnel, Chong had already been transferred to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud; he was dismissed and sent home on a charge of negligence.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Gong re-entered the Grand Secretariat and took charge of the Ministry of Personnel, Zhang Chong had already been transferred to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud; he was dismissed and sent home on a charge of negligence.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中，累官工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: During Wanli, through repeated promotions he reached Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign, through successive promotions he reached Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 林潤，字若雨，莆田人。

translations.literal: Lin Run, styled Ruoyu, was a native of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Run, styled Ruoyu, came from Putian.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十五年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the thirty-fifth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-fifth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授臨川知縣。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 以事之南豐，寇猝至，為畫計卻之。

translations.literal: While on business at Nanfeng, bandits suddenly arrived; he devised a plan and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: While on business at Nanfeng, bandits suddenly arrived; he devised a plan and repelled them.

sentences.zh: 征授南京御史。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed as Nanjing censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Nanjing censor.

sentences.zh: 嚴世蕃置酒召潤，潤談辨風生，世蕃心憚之。

translations.literal: Yan Shifan set out wine and summoned Run; Run spoke with eloquent force, and Shifan feared him in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shifan set out wine and summoned Lin Run; Lin Run spoke with eloquent force, and Yan Shifan inwardly feared him.

sentences.zh: 既罷，屬客謂之曰：「嚴侍郎謝君，無刺當世事。

translations.literal: After the banquet, he instructed a guest to tell him: "Vice Minister Yan thanks you, sir; do not satirize current affairs."
translations.idiomatic: After the banquet Yan Shifan instructed a guest to tell him: "Vice Minister Yan thanks you, sir; do not satirize current affairs."

sentences.zh: 」潤到官，首論祭酒沈坤擅殺人，置之理。

translations.literal: Run upon taking office first indicted Academician Director Shen Kun for unauthorized killing and had him prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Upon taking office Lin Run first indicted Academician Director Shen Kun for unauthorized killing and had him prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 已，劾副都御史鄢懋卿五罪，嚴嵩庇之，不問。

translations.literal: Thereafter he impeached Vice Censor-in-Chief Yan Maoqing on five counts; Yan Song shielded him, and no inquiry was made.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he impeached Vice Censor-in-Chief Yan Maoqing on five counts; Yan Song shielded him, and no inquiry was made.

sentences.zh: 伊王典楧不道，數遭論列不悛，潤復糾之。

translations.literal: Prince Yi Dianji was depraved, had repeatedly been indicted yet would not reform, and Run again impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi Dianji was depraved, had repeatedly been indicted yet would not reform, and Lin Run again impeached him.

sentences.zh: 典楧累奏辨，詆潤挾私。

translations.literal: Dianji repeatedly submitted memorials in his defense, slandering Run for acting from private motives.
translations.idiomatic: Dianji repeatedly submitted memorials in his defense, slandering Lin Run for acting from private motives.

sentences.zh: 部科交章論王抗朝命，脅言官。

translations.literal: Ministries and censorial offices submitted memorials in turn discussing the prince's resistance to court orders and intimidation of censorial officials.
translations.idiomatic: Ministries and censorial offices submitted memorials in turn denouncing the prince's resistance to court orders and intimidation of censorial officials.

sentences.zh: 世蕃納其賄，下詔責讓而已。

translations.literal: Shifan accepted his bribes, and the emperor issued only an edict of rebuke and censure.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shifan accepted his bribes, and the emperor issued only an edict of rebuke and censure.

sentences.zh: 潤因言宗室繁衍，歲祿不繼，請亟議變通。

translations.literal: Run therefore stated that the imperial clan had proliferated and annual stipends could not be sustained, requesting urgent deliberation on reform.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Run therefore stated that the imperial clan had proliferated and annual stipends could not be sustained, and requested urgent deliberation on reform.

sentences.zh: 帝為下所司集議。

translations.literal: The emperor had the responsible offices gather for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the responsible offices to gather for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 會帝用鄒應龍言，戍世蕃雷州，其黨羅龍文尋州。

translations.literal: It happened that the emperor, following Yinglong's proposal, sent Shifan to garrison at Leizhou and his associate Luo Longwen to Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the emperor, following Zou Yinglong's proposal, sent Yan Shifan to garrison at Leizhou and his associate Luo Longwen to Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 世蕃留家不赴。

translations.literal: Shifan remained at home and did not go to his posting.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shifan remained at home and did not go to his posting.

sentences.zh: 龍文一詣戍所，即逃還徽州，數往來江西，與世蕃計事。

translations.literal: Longwen once reached the garrison post, then fled back to Huizhou; many times he traveled back and forth in Jiangxi, scheming with Shifan.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Longwen reached the garrison post once, then fled back to Huizhou; many times he traveled back and forth in Jiangxi, scheming with Yan Shifan.

sentences.zh: 四十三年冬，潤按視江防，廉得其狀，馳疏言：「臣巡視上江，備訪江洋群盜，悉竄入逃軍羅龍文、嚴世蕃家。

translations.literal: In the winter of the forty-third year, Run inspected the river defenses, obtained the facts through investigation, and hurriedly submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject, inspecting the upper Yangtze, thoroughly inquired into river and sea bandits, and all have fled into the households of the deserter Luo Longwen and Yan Shifan."
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the forty-third year Lin Run inspected the river defenses, obtained the facts through investigation, and hurriedly submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject, inspecting the upper Yangtze, thoroughly inquired into river and sea bandits, and found that all have fled into the households of the deserter Luo Longwen and Yan Shifan."

sentences.zh: 龍文卜築深山，乘軒衣蟒，有負險不臣之心。

translations.literal: Longwen has chosen to build in deep mountains, rides in carriages and wears python robes, and has a heart of relying on perilous terrain and refusing subjection.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Longwen has chosen to build in the deep mountains, rides in carriages and wears python robes, and harbors a heart of relying on perilous terrain and refusing subjection.

sentences.zh: 而世蕃日夜與龍文誹謗時政，搖惑人心。

translations.literal: Shifan day and night with Longwen slanders current policy and shakes and deludes popular hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shifan day and night with Luo Longwen slanders current policy and sows unrest among the people.

sentences.zh: 近假名治第，招集勇士至四千余人。

translations.literal: Recently under the pretext of building a residence he has recruited warriors to more than four thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Recently under the pretext of building a residence he has recruited more than four thousand warriors.

sentences.zh: 道路恟懼，鹹謂變且不測。

translations.literal: Travelers on the road are in alarm and fear; all say rebellion may break out at any unpredictable moment.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers on the roads are alarmed and fearful; all say rebellion may break out at any unpredictable moment.

sentences.zh: 乞早正刑章，以絕禍本。

translations.literal: I beg that punishment be applied early according to law, so as to cut off the root of calamity.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that punishment be applied early according to law, so as to cut off the root of calamity.

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒，即詔潤逮捕送京師。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly enraged and immediately ordered Lin Run to arrest them and send them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was greatly enraged and immediately ordered Lin Run to arrest them and send them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 世蕃子紹庭官錦衣，聞命亟報世蕃，使詣戍所。

translations.literal: Shifan's son Shaoting held office in the Embroidered Uniform Guard; hearing the order he hastily reported to Shifan and had him go to his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan's son Shaoting held office in the Embroidered Uniform Guard; hearing the order he hastily reported to Shifan and had him go to his place of exile.

sentences.zh: 方二日，潤已馳至。

translations.literal: Within two days Lin Run had already galloped there.
translations.idiomatic: Within two days Lin Run had already galloped there.

sentences.zh: 世蕃猝不及赴，乃械以行，龍文亦從梧州捕至。

translations.literal: Shifan suddenly could not reach the exile post in time; he was shackled and taken away, and Longwen was also captured and brought from Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan could not reach the exile post in time; he was shackled and taken away, and Longwen was also captured and brought from Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 遂盡按二人諸不法事，二人竟伏誅。

translations.literal: Thereupon all the unlawful acts of the two men were fully investigated, and in the end both were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon all the unlawful acts of the two men were fully investigated, and in the end both were executed.

sentences.zh: 潤尋擢南京通政司參議，歷太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: Lin Run was soon promoted to vice director of the Nanjing Office of Transmission and later served as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Run was soon promoted to vice director of the Nanjing Office of Transmission and later served as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年以右僉都御史巡撫應天諸府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing he was appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of the prefectures of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Longqing reign he was appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of the Yingtian prefectures.

sentences.zh: 屬吏懾其威名，鹹震慄。

translations.literal: Subordinate officials feared his reputation for sternness and all trembled with dread.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate officials feared his reputation for sternness and all trembled with dread.

sentences.zh: 潤至，則持寬平，多惠政，吏民皆悅服。

translations.literal: When Lin Run arrived, he maintained leniency and fairness, enacted many benevolent policies, and officials and commoners alike were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Run arrived, he governed with leniency and fairness, enacted many benevolent policies, and officials and commoners alike were pleased and submitted.

sentences.zh: 居三年，卒官。

translations.literal: After three years in office he died in his post.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office he died in his post.

sentences.zh: 年甫四十。

translations.literal: He was only forty years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was only forty years old.

sentences.zh: 潤鄉郡興化陷倭，特疏請蠲復三年，發帑金振恤。

translations.literal: Lin Run's home prefecture Xinghua fell to Japanese pirates; he specially memorialized requesting a three-year remission of levies and the release of treasury funds for relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Run's home prefecture Xinghua fell to Japanese pirates, he specially memorialized requesting a three-year remission of levies and the release of treasury funds for relief.

sentences.zh: 鄉人德之。

translations.literal: The people of his homeland were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of his homeland were grateful to him.

sentences.zh: 喪歸，遮道四十里，為位祭哭凡三日。

translations.literal: When his coffin returned home, people blocked the road for forty li and set up places of mourning, weeping in sacrifice for three days in all.
translations.idiomatic: When his coffin returned home, people lined the road for forty li and set up places of mourning, weeping in sacrifice for three days in all.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：世宗非庸懦主也。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Emperor Shizong was no weak or cowardly ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Emperor Shizong was no weak or cowardly ruler.

sentences.zh: 嵩相二十余年，貪裛盈貫。

translations.literal: Song served as chief minister for more than twenty years, his greed overflowing to the full.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song served as chief minister for more than twenty years, his greed overflowing to the full.

sentences.zh: 言者踵至，斥逐罪死，甘之若飴，而不能得君心之一悟。

translations.literal: Remonstrators came one after another; they were dismissed, exiled, condemned, and put to death, yet they accepted it as sweet as honey—yet they could not win a single awakening of the ruler's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators came one after another; they were dismissed, exiled, condemned, and put to death, yet they accepted it as sweet as honey—yet they could not win a single awakening of the ruler's heart.

sentences.zh: 唐德宗言：「人謂盧杞奸邪，朕殊不覺。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong of Tang said: "People say Lu Qi was treacherous and wicked, yet I was wholly unaware of it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong of Tang said: "People say Lu Qi was treacherous and wicked, yet I was wholly unaware of it.

sentences.zh: 」各賢其臣，若蹈一轍，可勝嘆哉！

translations.literal: " Each ruler considers his minister worthy, as if treading the same track—how deeply lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: " Each ruler considers his minister worthy, as if treading the same track—how deeply lamentable!

sentences.zh: 世蕃之誅，發於鄒應龍，成於林潤。

translations.literal: The execution of Shifan began with Zou Yinglong and was completed by Lin Run.
translations.idiomatic: The execution of Yan Shifan began with Zou Yinglong and was completed by Lin Run.

sentences.zh: 二人之忠，非過於楊繼盛，其言之切直，非過於沈煉、徐學詩等，而大憝由之授首。

translations.literal: The loyalty of these two men did not surpass that of Yang Jisheng, nor were their words more cutting and direct than those of Shen Lian, Xu Xueshi, and others—yet because of them the great villain lost his head.
translations.idiomatic: The loyalty of these two men did not surpass that of Yang Jisheng, nor were their words more cutting and direct than those of Shen Lian, Xu Xueshi, and others—yet because of them the great villain lost his head.

sentences.zh: 蓋惡積滅身，而鄒、林之彈擊適會其時歟！

translations.literal: Surely accumulated evil destroys the man, and the impeachments of Zou and Lin happened to coincide with the moment!
translations.idiomatic: Surely accumulated evil destroys the man, and the impeachments of Zou and Lin happened to coincide with the moment!
